SBU Unit Chief Detained Over Ammunition Storage Violations After 35 Killed Near Kyiv
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:51:40 UTC
17:51:40 KST

The head of a Ukrainian Security Service (SBU) unit has been placed in custody on suspicion of violating ammunition storage requirements at a site near Kyiv where a Russian drone strike and subsequent explosions killed 35 people.
Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation said the official was responsible for storing weapons and ammunition at the facility in the village of Mila, located in the Bucha district of the Kyiv region.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Russian forces attacked warehouses belonging to a local enterprise at about 8:10 p.m. on Aug. 28. A unit from SBU used part of the premises.
The strike caused ammunition stored at the site to detonate, resulting in explosions and fires to spread to neighboring properties, investigators said.
Thirty-five people were killed, while one person remains missing, and 21 others were injured, including two children, police officers, and emergency workers. A nearby care home for older people sustained the heaviest damage.
According to investigators, the SBU unit stored weapons and ammunition in a former vegetable warehouse that did not have the required certification and failed to meet safety standards for explosive materials.
The facility was located less than 100 meters (328 feet) from nearby residential buildings.
Investigators also alleged that requirements governing the permitted quantity and dispersal of ammunition were not followed. Separating stored munitions is intended to reduce the risk of simultaneous detonation.
Russian Drone Strikes State-Owned Ukrnafta Gas Station in Kyiv, Smoke Seen Over City
The official was notified that he was suspected of failure to act by a military authority under martial law. The offense carries a possible prison sentence of up to 10 years.
Kyiv’s Pechersky District Court ordered the suspect to custody, but allowed the possibility of release on bail. Investigators are also examining whether security at the site was adequately supervised and whether measures were taken to strengthen its protection from aerial attacks.
Explosives and fire examinations have been ordered. Authorities are also working to identify other people whose actions or inaction may have contributed to the scale of the destruction.
The explosions damaged 14 apartment buildings and 191 private homes, with some structures completely destroyed. Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka territorial community, was among those killed.

Nearly 200,000 foreigners violating Russian laws barred from entering country — ministry

Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:51:09 UTC
17:51:09 KST

MOSCOW, September 10. /TASS/. The Russian Interior Ministry has barred approximately 200,000 foreigners who have violated Russian laws from entering the country, First Deputy Minister and Migration Service head Andrey Kikot told Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"As part of our preventive efforts, our units have barred entry to approximately 200,000 foreign nationals - to be precise, 197,000 - who have committed crimes and violated the law here. We have restricted their entry for a certain period of time," he noted.
According to Kikot, the number of cases involving the deportation of foreign citizens has increased by 85%. "We have deported around 100,000 people, 75,000 of whom were forcibly deported," the Migration Service head emphasized.
Kikot also pointed to an intensification of efforts to improve the quality of document checks for foreigners applying for legal status in Russia. "We have uncovered ten times more forged documents containing knowingly false information," he said.

Desogestrel contraceptives: 1.6 million women warned of tumour risk
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:50:34 UTC
17:50:34 KST

The French medicines agency (ANSM) urges women who take desogestrel contraceptives to seek medical advice if they develop suggestive symptoms, such as persistent headaches, visual disturbances or memory loss.
A low risk, but one that affects millions of women. In France, 1.6 million women who have taken a desogestrel-based contraceptive (Antigone, Cerazette, Elfasette and Optimizette...) will receive a letter informing them of an increased risk of developing a meningioma, France's National Agency for Medicines and Health Products Safety (ANSM) announced on Thursday. The health authority stresses, however, that this risk remains "low".
At the same time, around 90,000 doctors who have prescribed these medicines will also be notified.
ANSM recommends that the women concerned consult their doctor if they experience persistent headaches, visual disturbances, muscle weakness, problems with balance or speech, memory loss, or the onset or worsening of epileptic seizures. A brain MRI scan may then be prescribed.
A risk that increases with the length of treatment
Meningioma is a tumour that develops from the meninges, the membranes that surround the brain. Most often benign, it can nonetheless cause significant neurological problems depending on its size and location.
According to a study by the Epi-Phare public interest research group published in 2024, one woman in 67,000 who has taken desogestrel develops a meningioma linked to this contraceptive. After five years of treatment, this proportion rises to one woman in 17,000.
The risk is doubled after seven years of use compared with women who have not taken this contraceptive. However, it disappears one year after stopping treatment. Women over 45, as well as those who have previously taken for more than a year a progestogen regarded as high-risk, are particularly affected.
The risk would nonetheless remain far lower than that associated with other progestogens, such as Androcur, Lutényl, Lutéran, Colprone or Depo Provera, for which monitoring by brain imaging is systematically recommended.
"This risk is low, and bears no comparison with that of Androcur, which was 20 times higher after five years", says Isabelle Yoldjian, ANSM's medical director.
Do not stop contraception without medical advice
ANSM is calling on the women concerned not to stop their contraception without medical advice and is urging them to discuss the issue with their doctor, gynaecologist or midwife at their next consultation.
The health authority also reminds women that any contraception should be reassessed every year with a healthcare professional, depending on each woman's needs and state of health.
Following a request from ANSM, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) this summer approved the addition of the risk of meningioma to the patient information leaflets for these contraceptives.

Japan deploys choppers to Indonesia in 1st overseas firefighting mission
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:49:46 UTC
17:49:46 KST

Ahmad Adil, Faisal Mahmud
10 September 2026•Update: 10 September 2026
A Japanese ship carrying three CH-47 helicopters arrived in wildfire-hit Indonesia on Thursday, marking Tokyo's first overseas firefighting mission, Kyodo News reported.
The 8,900-ton Osumi-class transport ship Kunisaki arrived at Kijing Port in West Kalimantan with around 350 personnel.   
The helicopters will support the Indonesian military in aerial firefighting for about a week from Sunday.
The CH-47s will draw water from rivers and carry about five tons on each run before dumping it over fire-hit areas.   
"We will make every effort" to execute the mission to help the victims, a Japanese Defense Ministry official said.
Massive fires that broke out across Indonesia between January and July have burned around 2,000 square kilometers (772 square miles) of forests and peatland, according to Kyodo. Fires are still burning in several parts of the country, with the Indonesian military conducting aerial firefighting operations.
The deployment follows an agreement signed in May between Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and his Indonesian counterpart Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin to broaden defense cooperation, including joint training and disaster relief operations.
Meanwhile, Japan has also deployed Japan Air Self-Defense Force fighter aircraft to India for the first time.  
Indian Air Force and the Japan Air Self Defence Force are holding bilateral air exercise, "Veer Guardian-2026," which began Wednesday and will run through September at Air Force Station Jodhpur in western India.  
Indian Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, writing on US social media company X, called the maiden visit a “significant milestone” in the India-Japan defense partnership.  
"I am deeply encouraged to see that Japan-India defense cooperation is steadily developing through the accumulation of exchanges and joint training between frontline units," said Koizumi in a separate post.

Pro-Israel Democratic Sen. Fetterman speaks at a GOP midterm convention, did he switch sides?
Democratic Senator John Fetterman spoke to the Republican midterm convention via video Wednesday, an extraordinary escalation of the growing rupture between the Pennsylvanian and his party.
Fetterman’s decision is certain to stoke fears, already simmering among Democrats, that he will switch parties. Democrats need to pick up four GOP-held Senate seats in November to regain the majority. If Fetterman were to join the Republican Party, Democrats would need to pick up another seat to have control of the chamber.
Fetterman spoke for just over one minute in a recorded video introducing his fellow Pennsylvania senator, Republican Dave McCormick, whom Fetterman called "a great American."
He didn't criticise anyone by name but suggested Democrats are extremists, underscoring the message that Republicans are trying to drive home during their two-day rally in Dallas. The convention is meant to fire up the conservative base ahead of midterm elections, when the president's party has historically lost seats.
"I'm always going to stand with America," Fetterman said. "I'm always going to reject the extremes and socialism and that anti-American way of life."
Standing in front of a steel mill, Fetterman said he "will work with President Trump to fight and defend the steel way of life."
Fetterman has grown increasingly isolated from his party as he "obsessively" support of Israel's genocide of Gaza and criticizes left-wing candidates who are members of the Democratic Socialists of America. He’s often gone his own way in the Senate, voting with Republicans to end last year's shutdown, supporting several of President Donald Trump's nominees and opposing efforts to end the war in Iran.
Fetterman has repeatedly said he wouldn’t switch parties because of his support for labor unions, LGBTQ rights and other issues held dear by the left.
Even if he remains a Democrat, he would hold outsized power in his caucus if Democrats secure a narrow 51-49 majority that requires them to stick together unanimously to exercise their power.
"How great is John Fetterman?" McCormick said when the video wrapped up. "Thank you, Senator Fetterman, for your friendship. Thank you for your courage. And thank you for all you do for Pennsylvania."
Right after Fetterman's video finished, it was shared on a White House social media account with the caption, "Based John Fetterman."

Houthi threat to Red Sea expands with takeover of Mocha, potentially reshaping region - analysis
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:48:56 UTC
17:48:56 KST

After three days of escalating conflict in Yemen, where it appeared that the Saudi-backed government was making gains, the Houthis gained control of the city of Mocha on the Red Sea on Thursday.
The advance by the Houthis was anticipated. It also appears that although the Houthis suffered some setbacks on other fronts, this offensive could have wider implications for the strategic Red Sea Mandab Straits.
Mocha is a port city that is one of several important ports in Yemen. Along with Hodeidah, it plays a key role along the Red Sea coast. It also sits at the northern end of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. As such, this could potentially put the Iranian-backed Houthis closer to being able to close the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the way they have attempted to close the Strait of Hormuz.
Houthi control gives Iran greater influence
This would give Iran more influence in the region, even as Iran was appearing to lose out on many fronts. For instance, Iranian-backed proxies have faced setbacks in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria. They have also faced pressure to disarm in Iraq. The Houthis are one of the most powerful pro-Iranian groups remaining.
Reuters reported that the Houthis had taken Mocha on September 10. The full story of what is happening in Yemen remains to be seen because reports are not always accurate. What matters is that the Houthis are trying to increase their role along the Red Sea.
This comes amid several developments in Yemen and Saudi Arabia. The Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia this week as fighting increased in Yemen. Riyadh backs the government of Yemen against the Houthis. Saudi Arabia led an intervention in Yemen in 2015.
Now, Arab News in Saudi Arabia has reported that “Saudi civil defense issued an emergency alert for the south western province of Khamis Mushait to warn of potential danger for the fourth time in 24 hours.” The General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defense said: “The danger has been lifted from Khamis Mushayt Governorate. For your safety, continue to follow the instructions of the Civil Defense and completely avoid gatherings and photography. In case of emergencies, call the number (998).” The warning had been linked to the Houthi conflict.
The Houthis had claimed to target an airbase in this part of southern Saudi Arabia near Yemen. As such, the Kingdom was being cautious. This shows that the Houthis are not wary of continuing to target the Kingdom. This comes as Pakistan has expressed support for Saudi Arabia. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey recently signed onto a defensive pact. There are questions about whether the Houthi attacks might trigger wider support for Riyadh.
Pakistan expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia
Pakistan’s leader has expressed his “unwavering solidarity” with Saudi Arabia, after Houthi drone and missile attacks on civilian and energy facilities in the Kingdom left 73 people injured, Arab News noted. “At the same time, Pakistan’s Defense Minister Khawaja Asif said that a three-nation defense pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye could become operational in the event of aggression against the Kingdom.”
Many are watching closely to see if the Saudis will receive support from their new partners. Iran is also watching to see if the Houthis can continue to make gains and threaten the Bab al-Mandab strait. The threat of the Houthis may increase global insecurity and continue to roil energy markets. US President Donald Trump had said that he expects the conflict with Iran to wind down after the US mid-term elections. The high oil prices are expected to come down as well. The battles in Mocha could change this perception.
There are other issues that will affect the fate of Yemen and the Red Sea coast. Saudi Arabia has been backing the government forces in Yemen. However, the Saudis and the UAE have not agreed on policy in Yemen. This may present challenges for the frontlines around Aden and Mocha.
The Yemen government forces who oppose the Houthis face a challenge in that they control areas around the Houthis, but the Houthis control the high ground and also part of the coast. As such, the Houthis can shift forces along internal lines. The Yemen government can’t do this. They can’t move forces easily from Jawf, for instance, to Mocha. To do so would require a lot of logistics, and it’s not an easy task. As such, the Houthis enjoy some advantages in being able to shift resources from one front to another. Even when pressed, the Houthis will continue to enjoy this advantage.
The setbacks in Mocha illustrate how a forgotten and low-level conflict in Yemen can potentially reshape the region.

Quote: "Two people have been killed and two more injured. The enemy struck Dnipro again.
The same business that was already hit in the previous strike has been damaged once more. A fire has broken out."
Details: Later, Hanzha reported that the number of people injured had risen to five, among them a child.

Firefighters have since contained the blaze.
Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov added that the Russians had also hit an Oleina sunflower oil plant, which is owned by the American company Bunge.

AMDL circle plans new public life for milan’s palazzo litta
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:45:26 UTC
17:45:26 KST

amdl circle opens milan’s palazzo litta to the public
AMDL CIRCLE, founded by Michele De Lucchi, presents a strategic masterplan for Palazzo Litta in Milan that seeks to open the monumental spaces of the historic building to the public while retaining its institutional role. Commissioned by the Direzione regionale Musei nazionali Lombardia, which has managed the palace since early 2025, the plan reorganizes the 17th-century complex around exhibition, cultural, and administrative functions, proposing the restoration of currently unused areas and the reopening of its long-inaccessible Monumental Garden.
Located on Corso Magenta, Palazzo Litta is among Lombardy’s significant examples of Baroque architecture. Its core develops from a project by architect Francesco Maria Richini, commissioned by Bartolomeo III Arese in the first half of the 17th century. Later architectural and decorative interventions substantially altered the palace, with the most important transformation taking place in the mid-18th century, when the interiors of the piano nobile acquired the elaborate character associated with Lombard Baroque.
The building now accommodates the Milan offices of five institutions belonging to the Italian Ministry of Culture, including three superintendencies, the Direzione regionale Musei nazionali Lombardia, and the Museo nazionale dell’Arte Digitale. AMDL CIRCLE’s masterplan reorganizes their relationship with the parts of Palazzo Litta intended for cultural use. The Milan-based architecture studio‘s strategy separates circulation according to use, reorganizing vertical connections and horizontal distribution so that visitors and office users can move through the building without unnecessarily overlapping. The approach also allows spaces that have become disconnected from the contemporary life of the palace to acquire new roles.
the palazzo is among Lombardy’s significant examples of Baroque architecture | image by Chabe01, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
the masterplan reorganizes the palace around public access
At ground level, the Cortile d’Onore becomes the principal threshold between Palazzo Litta and the city. The courtyard is planned as an urban court open to the public, with a ticket office, bookshop, exhibition areas, spaces presenting the sites managed by the Direzione regionale Musei nazionali Lombardia, and a new multipurpose hall.
New elevators connect the courtyard to the piano nobile and the office areas, while a direct route provides access to the garden behind the palace. In the rear buildings, the plan introduces more operational functions, including a library, conservation laboratories, artwork storage, and the export office. Archives are distributed between the basement and attic spaces. The arrangement establishes the courtyard as a point of orientation and circulation, connecting public programs with the deeper operational infrastructure required to keep a cultural institution functioning.
On the piano nobile, exhibition and event spaces are organized around a circular visitor route beginning at the monumental staircase and continuing around the Cortile d’Onore. The plan also introduces backstage areas that are currently lacking, acknowledging the practical requirements of programming exhibitions and events within a historic building. The ministerial offices remain in the more internal portion of the first floor and on the second floor, while the third floor undergoes renovation to accommodate their expansion. Guest residences for institutional and cultural use occupy the side wings and attic. New building services, including air-handling units serving the piano nobile, heat pumps, and photovoltaic panels, are placed on the roofs of the internal buildings, in areas that are less visible and had already undergone reconstruction after World War II.
the Cortile d’Onore becomes the principal threshold between Palazzo Litta and the city | image via MoscaPartners
the Monumental Garden becomes part of Palazzo Litta again
The plan also proposes restoring the 19th-century garden on the north side of Palazzo Litta, which has long been inaccessible. The intervention brings the garden back into the visitor route and allows it to host cultural events outdoors. More broadly, the masterplan reorganizes the palace around its existing mix of historic, cultural, and institutional uses, aiming to make more of the building accessible while continuing to accommodate the Ministry of Culture offices.
For De Lucchi, the challenge is to adapt the Baroque building to contemporary life while preserving its historic elements and original typology. Palazzo Litta has already changed use several times, from aristocratic residence to offices and, later, to the current Ministry of Culture headquarters. The masterplan adds another layer to this history by introducing a more public role for the building.
the building now accommodates the Milan offices of five institutions | image via MoscaPartners
archives are distributed between the basement and attic spaces | image via MoscaPartners

Spanish intelligence warned of refugee flow before Ceuta crisis
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:42:04 UTC
17:42:04 KST

Publicly released Spanish government documents show that intelligence agencies warned the day before the migration crisis in Ceuta about social media posts calling for mass border crossings, the BBC writes.
The revelations emerged in declassified Spanish government documents after accusations that the government failed to provide full information about the crisis that took place in Spanish territory in North Africa in late July, when tens of thousands of migrants crossed the border from Morocco. Spain’s National Intelligence Service (CNI) warned officials in both Morocco and Ceuta on the 29th of July that groups had been set up on social media calling for migrants to cross the border the following day. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has insisted that the crisis was unforeseeable, but opposition parties have accused the government of misleading Spaniards.
Sánchez had previously told lawmakers that there was no information available to predict the scale of the migration crisis in the last days of July. At least 72,000 migrants arrived illegally in Ceuta from Morocco on the 30th and the 31st of July. Most swam by the border fence in the sea and at least 100 people died en route. Although most have been returned to Morocco, around 5,000 migrants remain in Spanish territory in makeshift camps, sleeping on the streets or on the beach, sparking widespread discontent among Ceuta residents. Locals have raised concerns about security, and in some places migrant shelters have been destroyed and aid delivery blocked.
In a report on the 29th of July, the CNI warned Moroccan intelligence that it had identified WhatsApp and Facebook groups encouraging migrants to travel to Spain by land and sea. The CNI said that about 180,000 people had received such messages. One of the messages said that anyone wishing to cross the border would have a last chance on the 30th of July, as Moroccan authorities would be busy celebrating the Feast of the Throne.
The CNI also warned government officials in Ceuta.
The CNI messages are part of a package of more than 40 documents related to the migration crisis in Ceuta. The documents were declassified as pressure mounted on Sanchez and speculation spread that Morocco had played a role in helping migrants cross the border. Leaked Spanish police reports in early September pointed to a Moroccan police role in the incident.
Meanwhile, Sanchez insists there is no evidence of Moroccan involvement in orchestrating the migration crisis. Shortly before the documents were released, Sanchez said that a mass influx of migrants was not expected. Opposition politicians have said that the declassified documents paint a different picture. Ester Muñoz, a member of the conservative Popular Party, said that the information was available and that they were directly responsible for the invasion of Ceuta and the lives lost.
Jorge Buxadé, a politician from the far-right Vox party, said on social media that the documents indicate that Sanchez and “his gang of criminals” should be brought before the Supreme Court for treason and crimes against national security.
The government insists that it acted on the information available.
Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares said he was unaware of reports that predicted the scale of the crisis. A government source said declassified documents showed that the information available before the crisis did not allow for such a large migration wave.
Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano, the Spanish government spokesman in Ceuta, said the WhatsApp messages were not an official warning or announcement and were nothing more than a simple exchange of information, referring to the messages sent to his office on the 29th of July.

Hong Kong to roll out plain cigarette packs from March, full enforcement by December
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:41:41 UTC
17:41:41 KST

Hong Kong to strip logos and branding from cigarette packs starting in March
Only brand and variant names in prescribed font will be permitted, printed in standardised plain brown on packs under changes to existing law
All logos, colourful designs and branding will be stripped from cigarette packs in Hong Kong under new rules that take effect in March next year as part of a fresh push to reduce smoking rates.
The Department of Health announced on Thursday that subsidiary legislation would require all retail packs of cigarettes, long cigarette boxes and specified cigars to drop brand logos and advertising elements.
Only brand and variant names in a prescribed font will be permitted, printed in standardised plain brown on the pack. Manufacturers will have until December next year to ensure their products meet the new rules.
Dr Manny Lam Man-chung, head of the Tobacco and Alcohol Control Office, said the measure would reduce the appeal of tobacco products, citing a 2023 Chinese University of Hong Kong study in which 79.8 per cent of smokers surveyed said plain packaging made cigarettes less attractive.
“The measure will weaken brand effects, stop consumers underestimating health risks and make the graphic health warnings more prominent and effective,” he said.
Lam said 27 countries and regions, including Australia, Canada and France, had adopted standardised packaging.

Teknofest to boost tourism in southeastern Türkiye

The southeastern province of Şanlıurfa is bracing for a surge in tourism as Teknofest, the largest aviation, aerospace and technology festival, prepares to draw massive crowds.
Organized by the Industry and Technology Ministry, the T3 Foundation and the Defense Technologies Engineering and Trade Inc., the event will run from Sept. 30 to Oct. 4, with state-run Anadolu Agency serving as its global communications partner.
Hotel occupancy rates in the city exceeded 95 percent ahead of the festival, Şanlıurfa Tourist Guides Chambers Union Audit Board Head Müslüm Çoban said. Professionals initially set a target of 1.5 million visitors for the 2025 and 2026 period but now expect to surpass 2 million, he said.
“There will be a huge influx to Şanlıurfa from all over Türkiye,” Çoban said, noting the city already draws significant interest due to the ongoing Taş Tepeler Project. The initiative covers prehistoric settlements surrounding the famous Göbeklitepe site, often called the zero point in time.
Festival attendees will explore historic locations and sample local cuisine, generating revenue for the accommodation, food and transportation sectors, he said. Şanlıurfa’s capacity extends beyond cultural tourism, he said.
The economic momentum is expected to spread across Mesopotamia, historically known as the cradle of civilization. Mardin province tourist guide Adar Poyraz said the autumn looks very promising as tourist density escalates.
Visitors arriving in Şanlıurfa will likely extend their trips to see the neighboring cities of Mardin and Diyarbakır, Poyraz said.
“We are in favor of organizing such festivals in the region; they are part of local development,” he said.
Teknofest is Türkiye’s premier aerospace and technology festival, launched to cultivate public interest in science and display defense capabilities. The event rotates through cities each year to engage all demographics in innovation.

'It's a real struggle against neo-Nazis': Behind the far-right's political rise in Germany

The stunning triumph of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in a German state election represents a true "challenge to democracy" and has shaken the country's Jewish community, said author and activist Dr. Ofer Waldman, speaking on the Haaretz Podcast
"It's the first time that a right‑extremist party has had such a landslide victory in Germany," said Waldman, who heads the Heinrich Boll Foundation office in Tel Aviv.
Haaretz writer and editor David Issacharoff, who joined Waldman on the podcast for a discussion of the election results, said that state of Saxony-Anhalt, which gave 44 percent of its vote to the controversial AfD party, is populated by voters who "feel abandoned, forgotten, and very isolated," blaming the state and mainstream parties for their situation and channeling their resentment in an extremist political direction.
This is worsened, both Waldman and Issacharoff said, by the fact that East Germany was not part of the post-Holocaust democracy education push in the West. "Keeping Jewish memory there is a real struggle of individuals in that state, and they're up against real forces of neo‑Nazis," Issacharoff noted,
Both commentators pointed to the contrast between the expressed deep worry and concern of the German Jewish community regarding AfD antisemitism, and the resounding "utter silence" coming from the Israeli government – together with comments from Israel's ambassador in Berlin during the election campaign that highlighted antisemitism on the left, while downplaying the AfD's positions.
"When Israel and its representative in Germany focus all the fire towards the left, then they're totally absolving the right from its responsibility for antisemitism. And when the representatives of the Jewish state say that, it matters in Germany," Issacharoff said.
Waldman added the source of the dissonance was "what is perceived as a mutual enemy" by Israel's far-right government.
"The AfD is perceived as the enemy of the Muslim community in Germany and, as such, a possible ally to the current Israeli administration," Waldman said.

Houthis seize key Yemeni port, close in on Red Sea chokepoint
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:39:50 UTC
17:39:50 KST

Iran-backed Houthi rebels have seized the Yemeni Red Sea port city of Mocha, bringing the group closer to controlling the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait as fighting with Saudi-backed forces intensifies and threatens to reopen a major front in Yemen’s long-running war, Yemeni government sources told Reuters on Thursday.
Three Yemeni government sources said the Houthis had taken control of Mocha, a historic port on Yemen’s southwestern coast. Government military sources also said Houthi forces were closing in on Dhubab, another coastal area directly along the Bab el-Mandeb, as they push to control Yemen’s Red Sea coastline.
The advance would give the Houthis greater leverage over one of the world’s most important shipping routes. The Bab el-Mandeb, which separates Yemen from Djibouti and Eritrea, connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is a key passage for oil, fuel and other commodities moving between Asia and Europe through the Suez Canal.
The fighting has taken on added significance as the six-month conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran disrupts another crucial energy route, the Strait of Hormuz. About 28 commodity vessels passed through the Bab el-Mandeb on Wednesday, roughly in line with the recent average, according to preliminary ship-tracking data.
The Houthi advance comes amid a sharp escalation in fighting in Yemen and across the Saudi border in recent days, raising fears of a return to full-scale war after a UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted years of fighting between the Houthis and forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognized government.
The Houthis launched one of their largest attacks on Saudi Arabia since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began in February, targeting an air base at Khamis Mushait and oil infrastructure in nearby cities. The Saudi-led coalition said at least 73 people were wounded in attacks on four southern Saudi cities.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said Wednesday that Saudi warplanes had carried out 54 strikes over the previous 12 hours in several parts of Yemen. The Houthis said strikes hit Jawf, Marib and Saada provinces near the Saudi border, as well as Taiz in the south and Hodeidah on the Red Sea coast. Saudi Arabia did not confirm the strikes. Saree warned that the attacks would “not go unanswered and unpunished.”
Saudi civil defense authorities issued repeated emergency alerts in Khamis Mushait, including four within 24 hours, before announcing an all-clear Thursday. The renewed clashes have opened what amounts to a second major front in the wider regional conflict and increased concerns about energy supplies already strained by fighting around the Strait of Hormuz.
Pakistan has meanwhile conveyed a Saudi warning to Tehran urging it to rein in the Houthis, according to Saudi, Pakistani and Iranian sources cited by Reuters. A senior Iranian official said Tehran responded that it does not control the group. Two Iranian sources, however, told Reuters that Tehran had instructed the Houthis last week to attack Saudi Arabia and promised additional funding and weapons, while Iranian Revolutionary Guard commanders traveled to Yemen to help coordinate the attacks.
The Houthis control Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, and most of the country’s populous north. Capturing Mocha and making further gains around the Bab el-Mandeb would significantly expand their position along the Red Sea at a time when disruptions to both of the region’s major maritime chokepoints are already driving fears over global energy supplies. Brent crude rose above $100 a barrel Wednesday for the first time since July as the widening regional conflict heightened concerns about further disruptions.

Macron calls for 'shared governance' of space at Paris summit
French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday called for the "shared governance" of space in a speech delivered at the two-day International Space Summit held in Paris. He also called on Europe to develop its own crewed spaceflight capability as part of the broader push to strengthen the continent's space sector.

Speaking at the two-day International Space Summit in Paris Thursday, French President Emmanuel Macron called for "shared governance" of space in a speech urging European nations to work together to build up their joint sovereign space capabilities.
“Outer space remains the only major global commons that is not subject to regulations that match the stakes,” he said. “Shared governance is necessary to address these challenges.”
He described Europe's space sector as "fragile", but insisted that it could become a major world player. Macron announced some €20 billion in investments for Europe's space industry, and urged the bloc to develop its own crewed spaceflight programme.
"France has a long-reaching and unique history when it comes to space," he said. "Space policy was always built through cooperation here."
Read more'Passengers or pilots?' Europe looks to challenge US dominance in space sector with €10 billion plan
Key figures from Europe’s space industry and other international players have converged on Paris to discuss how to advance the continent’s ambitions in a global market dominated by the United States.
The two-day International Space Summit that started Wednesday gathers officials, astronauts, researchers and industry leaders from about 120 countries to discuss the future of the space industry and pursue potential business deals.
European nations have sought to build up their sovereign space capabilities since 2022 and Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which highlighted how Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications service has become both a critical partner for Kyiv and a potential vulnerability.
“For Europe there’s a lot at stake,” the director general of the European Space Agency (ESA), Josef Aschbacher said. “Satellites are really being utilised day in, day out. It’s what we call a critical infrastructure, therefore extremely important for every citizen.”

The United States remains the global leader in the space sector, with NASA conducting major exploration missions and overseeing the Artemis program, which aims to establish a human presence on the moon.
Musk’s rocket company, SpaceX, has transformed the commercial launch industry by making reusable rockets operational, lowering costs and increasing the frequency of launches.
Meanwhile, Amazon launched its first internet satellites in 2025. The company plans to deploy more than 3,200 satellites to provide broadband service around the world. Amazon's founder Jeff Bezos also established the rocket company Blue Origin.
SpaceX and Blue Origin cancelled plans to attend the Paris summit, the French government said. News outlet Politico reported that the White House had urged US space companies not to attend because it could appear to support European Union policies.

Ukraine's Zelenskyy arrives in Canada seeking air support
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10

Ukraine's Zelenskyy arrives in Canada seeking air support
September 10, 2026
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Calgary late on Wednesday for "important meetings and agreements" with Canadian officials, including Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Zelenskyy arrived on the heels on attending King Harald V's funeral in Norway, where his plane had been delayed by a drone incursion.
The Ukrainian leader is in the middle of a flurry of trips and meetings to shore up his country's defenses for the cold winter months.
"The main focus will be on supporting Ukraine in protecting our skies and preparing for the winter," Zelenskyy said in a social media post before leaving.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement that the visit "will focus on shared priorities between Canada and Ukraine, including deepening defense, economic, and energy cooperation."
Carney's statement added Canada "remains steadfast in our commitment to support Ukraine's defense, recovery, and reconstruction."
Zelenskyy had also signaled a desire to meet with US President Donald Trump on the matter before the end of September.
Since Russia's invasion in 2022, Moscow has consistently increased attacks on fuel and heating infrastructure in Ukraine in the autumn and winter.
What is happening on the battlefield?
Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery in the Yamalo-Nenets region overnight, as well as a seaport in Dagestan, Zelenskyy said. He added that other unnamed sited critical to Russia's war industry had also been hit.
Alexander Gusev, governor of Russia's Voronezh region, said that one woman in the town of Borisoglebsk had been killed by falling drone debris overnight and that at least 19 drones had been destroyed while flying over the region.
The Russian Defense Ministry said a total of 448 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight.
In Ukraine, Russian attacks hit buildings owned by a major food producer in Dnipro, killing at least two according to local officials.

Iceland to propose whaling ban next February, leaving Norway and Japan isolated
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:37:27 UTC
17:37:27 KST

Iceland to propose whaling ban next February, leaving Norway and Japan isolated
- Iceland will propose a permanent ban on commercial whaling in February, leaving only Norway and Japan continuing the practice.
- The Bill has strong political and public support, citing ethical, legal, and conservation reasons to protect vulnerable fin whales.
- Norway resumed whaling in 1993, Iceland in 2006, and Japan resumed after leaving the International Whaling Commission in 2019; indigenous whaling remains allowed under the moratorium.
AI generated
COPENHAGEN – Iceland’s government will submit a Bill in February 2027 to ban whaling, a move that would leave Norway and Japan as the only two countries in the world to continue commercial whaling.
Whaling in Iceland has sparked years of protests from animal welfare campaigners and Hollywood celebrities.
The Bill will include “a permanent ban on whaling”, the government, which has a majority in Parliament, said on its website late on Sept 9.
In the 2026 hunting season, which runs from June to around the end of September, 80 fin whales were caught as at Sept 9, according to Humane World for Animals, an animal welfare group that tracks the catches. The quota allows 150 fin whales to be killed this year.
“There is considerable political and public support for this Bill to ban commercial whaling, and compelling ethical, veterinary, legal and conservation reasons to hope it succeeds,” said Wendy Higgins, a Humane World for Animals spokeswoman.
Fin whales, the primary target of Iceland’s whaling industry, are classified by the International Union for Conservation of Nature as vulnerable.
In 2024, Iceland’s interim government issued a five-year licence to its sole remaining whaling company.
Only Iceland, Norway and Japan have conducted commercial whaling in recent years, according to the International Whaling Commission’s catch list.
Norway resumed commercial whaling in 1993 and Iceland in 2006, despite an international moratorium that took effect in 1986 to protect whale populations.
Japan withdrew from the International Whaling Commission in 2019 and resumed commercial whaling in its territorial waters and exclusive economic zone.
The moratorium allows indigenous peoples in certain parts of the world, such as Greenland and Alaska, to hunt whales because whale products play a vital role in their nutritional and cultural lives. REUTERS

Tens of thousands attend King Harald V’s funeral in Norway
Finland
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
11:36:40 EEST
17:36:40 KST

Tens of thousands of people lined the streets of Oslo on Wednesday for the funeral of King Harald V, bringing 13 days of national mourning to an end and marking the start of the reign of his son, King Haakon VIII.
Harald died on 28 August aged 89 after 35 years on the throne. More than 46,000 people had filed past his coffin during the days before the funeral.
The funeral procession travelled from the Royal Palace to Oslo Cathedral, with Harald's coffin carried on an artillery carriage under the royal banner. A 21-gun salute sounded from Akershus Fortress as the procession crossed the centre of the capital.
King Haakon VIII walked behind his father's coffin with Crown Princess Ingrid Alexandra, Prince Sverre Magnus and Princess Märtha Louise. Queen Sonja and Queen Mette-Marit followed by car.
About 1,900 military personnel formed a guard of honour along the route, while thousands of spectators gathered behind barriers.
Norway observed a minute's silence before the funeral service at Oslo Cathedral. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and parliament speaker Masud Gharahkhani were among those who addressed the congregation.
"He struck a balance between being stately and being down-to-earth," Støre said. "He made Norway greater. He spoke of a 'we' in Norway where everyone is there for each other."
The service brought together royal families and political leaders from Europe and beyond. Britain's Prince William represented King Charles III, while Princess Anne, godmother to King Haakon, attended in a private capacity.
Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf and Denmark's King Frederik X attended alongside Spain's King Felipe, the Netherlands' King Willem-Alexander and other members of European royal families. Jordan's King Abdullah II and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky were also among the guests.
Finnish President Alexander Stubb attended the private burial ceremony at Akershus Fortress.
Four Norwegian F-35 fighter jets flew over Oslo Cathedral after the service. One aircraft separated from the formation in a military tribute to Harald, who served as Norway's head of state and commander-in-chief.
The coffin then travelled to Akershus Fortress, where members of the royal family and invited guests attended a private service at the Palace Chapel.
Harald was laid to rest in the Royal Mausoleum, where his parents, King Olav V and Crown Princess Märtha, and his grandparents, King Haakon VII and Queen Maud, are also buried.
Flags across Oslo were raised from half-mast following the burial as a royal salute sounded from Akershus Fortress. Church bells rang across Norway for an hour.
King Haakon and the royal family then returned to the Royal Palace and appeared on its balcony before crowds gathered outside.
Haakon, 53, became king on his father's death. He had served as crown prince since 1991 and has assumed the throne alongside his wife, Queen Mette-Marit.
The new king and queen later hosted a private reception at the Royal Palace for foreign heads of state, visiting royals, Norwegian officials and members of the royal family.
HT

Voronezh Woman Killed and Caspian Seaport Hit in Ukrainian Drone Strikes
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:36:07 UTC
17:36:07 KST

A Ukrainian drone attack in the southern Voronezh region killed a woman, local authorities said, as other strikes across the country damaged infrastructure and wounded dozens of people.
Voronezh Region Governor Alexander Gusev said a woman identified only as having been born in 1983 was killed when a drone crashed into a house in the town of Borisoglebsk. Two others were injured, he said.
In a separate seaborne drone attack on the Black Sea city of Sochi, 28 people were injured, emergency officials said.
Further to the east, in the North Caucasus republic of Dagestan, acting regional head Fyodor Shchukin said Ukrainian strikes sparked fires at a seaport and a theater in the capital city of Makhachkala. He said both fires were quickly put out.
Unverified reports said the Makhachkala Commercial Sea Port, Russia’s only deep-water port on the Caspian Sea, was hit in the attack.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky later confirmed his military struck a seaport in Dagestan. He said several sites were also hit in the Moscow, Astrakhan, Bryansk and Voronezh regions.
Meanwhile, in the southwestern Belgorod region, authorities said Ukrainian strikes over the past 24 hours had killed a man and wounded 13 others.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 448 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Wednesday night and Thursday morning.

10 September 2026•Update: 10 September 2026
The highly anticipated GITEX Ai Türkiye continued with its second day in Istanbul as global technology leaders, investors and startups explored major artificial intelligence (AI) opportunities and strategic partnerships.
The global event, hosted by the Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye Investment Office and the Industry and Technology Ministry, opened its doors on Wednesday at the Istanbul Expo Center.
Anadolu Agency acts as the global communication partner for the event where startups, investors and tech giants gathered to expand into new markets and develop collaborations.
Investment Office Communications Department Head Gokhan Yucel and GITEX Vice President Bilal Alrais delivered the opening speeches on the first day.
A prominent panel titled "The 1GW Countdown" discussed Türkiye's AI strategy to reach at least one gigawatt of installed data center capacity by 2030.
Participants evaluated the necessary implementation models to transform this target into operational computing capacity while addressing risks like permit processes and grid connection schedules.
Speakers explored how enterprise AI will shape the future beyond 2027 and how leaders can prepare for this massive digital transformation.
Istanbul Chamber of Industry Head Erdal Bahcivan questioned whether the current enterprise versions can cope with the real artificial intelligence world during his speech.
Women and Democracy Foundation board of trustees Chair Sumeyye Erdogan Bayraktar attended a session focusing on women, leadership and human-centric innovation in the digital era.
Another panel focused on smart factories, evaluating the transition from early pilot applications to scalable artificial intelligence use in production lines, quality control and planning.
Experts discussed how automated agents reshape corporate operations across customer service, finance and human resources while highlighting necessary security and governance measures.
A session on accelerating retail transformation covered the integration of smart systems into global retail operations and the delivery of real-time personalized e-commerce experiences.
The first day concluded with a panel on building an ecosystem featuring TUBITAK ULAKBIM Director Mehmet Mirat Satoglu, BSC AI Factory Türkiye Project Leader Feyza Eryol and TUBITAK BILGEM AI Institute Director Mehmet Haklidir.
The event hosts 24 companies under the Turcorn 100 Program, which aims to carry Türkiye's unicorn and growth-stage companies to international markets.
Global technology giants including Google Cloud, HPE, NVIDIA, ASUS, Dell Technologies, Huawei, SAP and TrendAI also participate in the massive exhibition.

SBI suspects SBU official of organizing ammunition storage in Mila village near Kyiv
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
11:32:55 EEST
17:32:55 KST

Officers of the State Bureau of Investigation (SBI) have notified a department head in charge of supply and logistics at the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) of suspicion for overseeing the arrangement and operation of an artillery ammunition depot in the village of Mila near Kyiv.
"It has been established that when deciding to locate the warehouse in a former vegetable storage facility, he failed to take all control measures regarding the security of storing explosives and ammunition. In addition, the warehouse was illegally located near residential buildings. The premises not only failed to meet requirements for weapons storage facilities, but its placement was not coordinated with relevant law enforcement structures and air defense units. The official also failed to take measures to minimize the risks of simultaneous destruction of a large quantity of ammunition by the enemy," the press service of the SBI reported.
Russian unmanned aerial vehicles launched a strike on the facility, triggering ammunition detonation and a fire that spread to neighboring premises.
As a result of the detonation, 35 people were killed. In addition, 191 private residential houses, 14 apartment buildings, a police station, garages, a restaurant, a nursing home, a shop, and a logistics center were damaged, as well as 24 vehicles, including a police service car and a fire truck.
The official has been notified of suspicion of inaction of military authority committed under martial law (Part 4 of Article 426 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine).
Pechersky District Court of Kyiv remanded him in custody as a preventive measure with an alternative of bail.
The article's sanction provides for punishment in the form of imprisonment for a term of up to 10 years.
His name and the specific department he headed have not been disclosed.
As reported by the Prosecutor General's Office of Ukraine on Thursday, after a similar tragedy in the city of Vyshneve (Kyiv region), measures were initiated to liquidate the depot and remove the ammunition, but as of August 28, when the occupiers attacked the storage facilities with drones, these measures had not been completed. It is emphasized that the depot was located less than 100 meters from residential buildings, and requirements regarding the permissible quantity of ammunition and its dispersal—intended to reduce the risk of simultaneous detonation and damage to surrounding facilities—were not observed.
"The investigation is also examining the circumstances of improper security control over the facility and the failure to take measures to strengthen its air defense cover. Forensic explosives and fire safety evaluations have been ordered in the proceedings... All circumstances are being established, as well as other individuals whose decisions, actions, or inaction may have affected the scale of the consequences of the Russian attack," the agency reported.
Earlier, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that such tragedies are unacceptable, especially after a similar event occurred in Vyshneve near Kyiv, calling it the result of "terrible negligence by those who stored explosives right next to people." He reported that criminal proceedings had been opened regarding the incident and called for a full investigation into all the facts of what transpired.

Thais take to streets in rare protest against Israel: ‘not for sale’

Thais take to streets in rare protest against Israel: ‘not for sale’
The protest follows months of complaints about illegal landholding, cultural disrespect and proliferation of Israeli religious houses
3-MIN READ3-MIN
10
 Listen
Hundreds of Thais, led by a veteran political activist, rallied outside the Israeli Embassy in Bangkok on Thursday in a rare public protest against a group of foreign nationals.
The protest follows months of complaints about illegal landholding, disrespect towards local culture and proliferation of religious houses for Israelis, echoing those made by some locals in the Philippines and Sri Lanka.
Israelis have been flocking to Thailand since the war on Gaza that followed the October 7 Hamas assault on their country. Many are service personnel from the Israel Defence Forces seeking respite from a war that has killed over 70,000 Palestinians and left around 2 million more stranded on the strip without food and water.
In a country with hair-trigger sensitivities over sovereignty, allegations that swathes of prime Thai land have been sold illegally to Israelis have raised uproar. Disputes between Thais and Israelis – mainly on the islands of Phangan and Samui and the mountain retreat of Pai – over non-payment of bills, public misbehaviour and pro-Palestine flags at some Thai businesses have gone viral, adding to the tensions.
Thursday’s protest – which saw an angry crowd waving a sea of Thai tricolours and banners saying “Save Thailand”, “Thailand Is Not For Sale” and “This is Not The Promised Land”, alongside some plainly antisemitic placards – was led by firebrand Sondhi Limthongkul.

Timeline: How a Russian drone nearly hit Zelenskyy's plane in Moldova
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:31:42 UTC
17:31:42 KST

Russia’s latest drone incursion into Moldova and NATO airspace comes as Moscow increasingly deploys jet-powered attack drones, blurring the line between traditional UAVs and low-cost cruise missiles and making them much harder to intercept.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s plane was preparing to leave Chișinău for Oslo on Tuesday afternoon when Moldova’s military detected an unmanned aerial vehicle in the country’s airspace.
What initially appeared to be another Russian drone incursion took on greater significance the following day, when Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre revealed that Zelenskyy’s plane had almost been hit by a drone.
“His flight was almost hit by a drone when it was taking off from Moldova. That is the reality he lives in,” Støre told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK.
The timeline shows how the events unfolded.
Moldovan military first detected an unidentified unmanned aerial vehicle at 4:20 pm EEST (3:20 CEST).
Moldovan officials confirmed to Euronews that the country’s airspace was closed shortly after 4:30 pm.
“The airspace was closed to protect the aircraft flying over Moldova at the time - three departures and four arrivals were delayed as a result.”
By 4:37 pm, Romania’s Defence Ministry said the drone crossed into Romanian — and therefore NATO — airspace.
Two minutes later two Spanish F-18 fighter jets deployed as part of NATO’s enhanced Air Policing mission took off to monitor it.
The jets did not intercept the drone. Romanian radar continued to track it until 5:02 pm, when contact was lost.
Five minutes later at 5:07 pm the drone was detected again over Moldova, where it later crashed about 25 km east of the Romanian border.
According to Moldovan officials, the flight restrictions were lifted after 5:20 pm, when authorities confirmed the drone had come down and exploded near Mihăilenii Vechi, in the Râșcani district, about 160 km from Chișinău International Airport.
“For the same reason, the plane of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy took off from Chișinău International Airport later than scheduled," officials said.
According to monitoring channels, Zelenskyy’s plane took off from Chișinău around 5:57 pm.
For much of Russia's full-scale war in Ukraine that began in early 2022, Zelenskyy has travelled abroad primarily through Poland, with Rzeszów serving as a regular departure point.
In recent months, however, his presidential aircraft has also begun using Chișinău more frequently for foreign trips.
What type of drone was it?
The exact model of the drone involved in Moldova and Romania has not been officially established.
Ukrainian open-source monitoring channels identified it as a Geran-4, one of Russia’s newer jet-powered attack drones.
The Geran-4 and Geran-5 are among the newest additions to Russia’s expanding Geran family, although they differ significantly in design and capabilities.
The Geran-4 has a wingspan of about three metres and is roughly 3.5 metres long. Its maximum take-off weight is around 450 kilograms.
According to Ukrainian military intelligence, the Geran-4 can reach speeds of up to 500 km/h and carry a warhead weighing between 50 and 90 kilograms.
Russia has recently stepped up its use of jet-powered drones, including in complex barrages alongside ballistic and cruise missiles designed to overwhelm Ukrainian air defences.
Their speed makes them much harder to intercept than conventional Shahed-type drones, particularly for the mobile fire groups and other relatively inexpensive systems Ukraine has relied on to counter slower-moving UAVs.
Ukraine is instead forced to use scarce and considerably more expensive air-defence missiles against the faster threats, putting additional pressure on already limited interceptor stocks.
Several Ukrainian companies have reportedly begun testing missiles specifically designed to shoot down the new jet-powered Geran models.

Consequences of Kiev's provocation against UK diplomats could have been grave — expert
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:31:06 UTC
17:31:06 KST

MOSCOW, September 10. /TASS/. The consequences of a potential provocation by Ukrainian special services against British diplomats in Moscow could have been severe, Vladimir Nechayev, a veteran of the Soviet Unions’ KGB counterintelligence service has said.
"Ukrainian special services are overdoing it; in this instance, they aimed the spearhead of the entire operation at the British diplomatic mission. Had it succeeded, it could have led to very serious consequences, potentially even escalating to a military conflict between Russia and the UK," he said in a video released by the FSB.
Nechayev explained that the essence of the Ukrainian special services' scheme involved gathering personal data - ranging from the British ambassador in Moscow down to every other staff member of the country's diplomatic mission in Russia - via a security guard at the British embassy.
"The transfer of such highly detailed information could have resulted in dire consequences, including terrorist attacks and physical or psychological harm to these individuals. Naturally, following a well-worn script, Ukraine planned to subsequently target accusations against the Russian side. It was yet another crude provocation - and a clumsily fabricated one," Nechayev noted.
Earlier, the FSB announced the detention of a former security guard at the British embassy in Moscow who turned out to be an SBU agent; he had been gathering information on British diplomats on the instructions of Ukrainian blogger Dmitry Karpenko (using the alias Apostol Dmitry). Ukrainian special services planned to use this information to prepare terrorist attacks against the ambassador and other British diplomats, intending to subsequently blame Moscow and draw Britain into a direct armed conflict with Russia.

Cop31: Forget climate pledges, countries like Nepal need actual cash
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:30:06 UTC
17:30:06 KST

Cop31: Forget climate pledges, countries like Nepal need actual cash
No payout from the loss and damage fund has reached vulnerable nations. Cop31 must focus on delivering the money already promised
Every climate summit now runs on the same illusion: the next pledge will be the one that finally saves us. It will not. The money the rich world has promised the poor world is not coming at anything like the scale advertised, and pretending otherwise has become the main business of climate diplomacy.
Late last month, a melting glacier gave way on the edge of the Himalayas and sent a wall of rock and water down the valley, burying whole settlements and leaving a country in national mourning.
Set that against how quickly everything else moves. In the same few weeks, the calendar filled with gatherings: a climate finance week in Istanbul, a week of chief-executive meetings in Baku, Azerbaijan, and a Pacific leaders’ summit in Palau. There is no shortage of mobilisation, only not the kind that moves money from one account to another.
A fund that cannot send US$20 million to a grieving country in the time it takes to hold three high-level meetings is not yet a fund. It is a promise with a letterhead.

Salboni land scam case: Bengal CID detain's Abhishek Banerjee's PA

Roy had earlier approached the Supreme Court after the Calcutta High Court denied him anticipatory bail on August 3 (Photo: PTI).
NEW DELHI: The Bengal CID on Thursday detained TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee’s PA, Sumit Roy. This came after the Supreme Court rejected Roy's anticipatory bail plea in the Salboni land scam caseA bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also lifted its August 6 order that had protected Roy from arrest, allowing his detention by the Bengal CID.The court heard arguments from senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, representing Roy, and solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the West Bengal government, before rejecting the plea.Roy had earlier approached the Supreme Court after the Calcutta High Court denied him anticipatory bail on August 3, in the case being investigated by the Salboni police.
The case concerns allegations that West Bengal government land was sold and the proceeds were deposited into the TMC's account. Roy faces charges relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy.The prosecution had opposed interim protection for Roy, arguing that his custodial interrogation was necessary.The high court had also been told that the investigation had uncovered forged title deeds linked to government land. The prosecution alleged that the land was transferred with the involvement of local political leaders and influential persons.

Tighter EU investment conditions targeted at China are 'fair', says expert
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:29:26 UTC
17:29:26 KST

Alicia García-Herrero, an economist at the Bruegel think tank, says new EU legislation to limit the subsidies foreign companies investing in Europe can receive is “fair”, despite facing criticism.
The European Parliament is proposing to close the EU market to Chinese investment in sectors where Beijing is dominant, going further than the European Commission’s proposal. García-Herrero warns that if the Chinese government wants to compete through subsidies, European companies “won’t have a chance” against Chinese firms.
A few months ago, the European Commission unveiled a proposal allowing EU public authorities to favour European companies in public procurement for key public services such as energy, water, railways, ports, airports and postal services.
The move clearly targets Chinese companies in a market valued at €2 billion annually. It comes as European policymakers seek to shield the bloc’s market from China amid heated trade negotiations, with the EU facing a trade deficit with Beijing of roughly €1 billion a day.

Spain endures 61 days of heatwave and records its hottest summer on record
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:27:59 UTC
17:27:59 KST

Spain's weather agency has confirmed that Spaniards have already endured 61 days of heatwave conditions so far this year, more than in any other year.
Spain has surpassed the scorching summer of 2022, with a total of 61 heatwave days endured this year, compared with 41 previously, according to the State Meteorological Agency (Aemet).
The summer of 2026 has also recorded an average temperature of 24.5°C, making it the hottest since records began in 1961 and surpassing last year, 2025, by 0.3°C, and 2.4°C above the long-term average.
Aemet recalls that the 10 hottest summers on record have all occurred in the 21st century, and seven of the eight warmest have taken place since 2015. The agency also warns that the meteorological summer keeps getting longer.
"At the end of May, temperatures typical of July were recorded across large areas of the country. And then, in September, already in the meteorological autumn, there was another heatwave which, provisionally, ran from the 2nd to the 7th, lasting six days and affecting 16 provinces."
September heat, rainfall and wildfires: Spain outlook
Only in four other years has a month of September (1987, 1988, 2006 and 2016) seen such extreme heatwaves, more typical of the height of summer.
The heavy winter rains have meant that Spanish reservoirs have remained in very good condition after the summer season, with an average level of 62.58 per cent despite tourist pressure, and above half of their capacity in basins that are usually under stress, such as the Júcar, Segura, Andalusian Mediterranean and Catalan catchments.
Even so, this has not spared the country from suffering, as in the rest of Europe, large-scale fires that have exposed the lack of forest fire prevention and of sufficient personnel with good working conditions, in regions such as Madrid, Aragón or Castilla y León.

====================================================================================================

August hottest month ever recorded globally: EU monitor
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:27:00 UTC
17:27:00 KST

Picture taken on August 14, 2026 with a drone shows the Pfalzgrafenstein Castle on an island in the dried-up river Rhine in Kaub, western Germany. (AFP Photo)
The EU’s climate monitor said on Sept. 10 that August was the hottest single month ever recorded globally, with ocean temperatures also reaching unprecedented highs as western Europe capped its warmest summer.
In response to the assessment by the Copernicus Climate Change Service, the U.N. warned that until humanity weaned off fossil fuels, the planet would only push deeper into uncharted territory.
Copernicus observations go back to 1940 but other evidence, such as ice cores, tree rings and coral skeletons, allow scientists to place today’s climate against a much longer historical context.
“Humans haven’t seen temperatures as hot as today for, arguably, at least the last 100,000 years,” Samantha Burgess from the European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which oversees Copernicus, told AFP.
Global average air temperatures in August were 16.96 degrees Celsius, Copernicus said, surpassing by 0.01 degrees the previous all-time monthly record set in July 2023. Copernicus said it considered the two months joint-highest given the narrow difference.
Scientists say that human activity, primarily the burning of coal, oil and gas, has warmed the planet by roughly 1.4 degrees since pre-industrial times and increased the severity and likelihood of extreme weather.
Yet heat-trapping greenhouse gas emissions rose to new highs in 2025.
“The evidence is irrefutable: This is the spiraling price of humanity’s fossil fuel addiction, and the global climate crisis it is fueling,” United Nations climate chief Simon Stiell said of the Copernicus report.
Global sea surface temperatures also set a new daily high and tied equal-hottest for August, extending a three-month streak of record-breaking warmth across the world’s oceans.
More than 90 percent of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gas emissions has been absorbed by the oceans, sparing land from warming but at severe cost to marine life, reefs and coastal communities.
Records tumbled in overheated basins like the Atlantic and Mediterranean and also the tropical Pacific, where the strongest El Nino weather pattern in the modern era is fast accumulating strength.
Scientists expect records to keep falling in the months ahead as this “super” El Nino approaches peak intensity around December and for 2027, and maybe even 2026, to become the hottest years ever observed.
Copernicus also said that August “marked the end of western Europe’s warmest summer” that surpassed the long-standing record set in 2003.
The June to August season was defined by severe, back-to-back heat waves that shut schools, dried up rivers and primed the land for devastating wildfires.
Between mid-July and mid-August, the continent’s EuroMomo monitoring platform estimated that Europe saw more than 32,000 excess deaths.

Singapore PM increases his salary by $1.1 million amid first government pay raise in 15 years
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:26:48 UTC
17:26:48 KST

Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced the salary increases in parliament on Tuesday, the first for ministers in 15 years. Wong's own benchmark paycheck is set to rise 64 percent to 3.6 million Singapore dollars (€2.4 million) a year.
Singapore’s ministers, already among the world’s highest-paid, are getting a raise for the first time in 15 years, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said, explaining that the government cannot attract top talent into politics if salaries remain unchanged.
Wong told Parliament on Tuesday that under a revised salary framework, the benchmark annual pay for a minister at the lowest grade will rise to 1.8 million Singapore dollars (€1.2 million), from Sg$1.1 million (€747,564). The prime minister’s benchmark salary will jump to Sg$3.6 million (€2.4 million) from Sg$2.2 million (€1.5 million), he said.
Ministers' pay has long been politically sensitive in the city-state, especially amid cost-of-living concerns and a 2025 median gross monthly income of Sg$5,775 (€3924) for fully employed residents, according to government figures.
The increases were recommended by an independent committee.
Wong said, however, the ministers will not immediately get the full salary increases. They will receive a one-off adjustment of up to 9 percent from October 15, depending on individual circumstances, including performance.
Wong also said he would donate his entire salary increase to charity for the next five years.
Mixed reactions among Singaporeans
Singaporeans expressed mixed reactions on Wednesday over hefty pay raises for political leaders, with some saying the demands of governing justified the bump while others questioned their scale and called for transparency.
May Goh, 69, a retiree from the semiconductor industry, said the ministers deserve the increases. "I think their responsibilities are very high. They are doing a good job so far compared to other countries," she said.
A 32-year-old cybersecurity employee in the business district said she "honestly" thought the increases were fair. "They are basically the CEOs of the political world," she said.
Others were more guarded. The increases are "very steep", said a 26-year-old information technology consultant.
"When you see such a huge salary increase, it puts into perspective, like 'wow that's quite a lot'. We don't even spend that much," he said.
A 69-year-old retiree, while voicing support, said he wanted more transparency with the numbers.
"I wish they were a bit clearer and more transparent about these numbers, including bonuses," he said.

Centre tells SC it is open to tougher labels on packaged foods high in sugar, salt or fat
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
08:25:45 UTC
17:25:45 KST

Supreme Court Justice JB Pardiwala questioned why the FSSAI was taking a two-phased approach.
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday told the Supreme Court that it was willing to consider stronger warning labels on packaged food, opening the door to tighter front-of-pack labelling rules that could have a significant impact on the country's packaged food industry.The issue concerns a proposed system under which food packets would carry prominent red hexagonal warnings to alert consumers when products contain high levels of nutrients linked to health risks, reported news agency Reuters.The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had recently proposed introducing the labelling system in two phases. Under the initial plan, a product would get a red warning symbol if it crossed the prescribed limits in at least two of three categories, namely added sugar, salt or saturated fat. Tighter provisions were to follow in the second phase.Health experts and activists have opposed this approach, arguing that requiring a product to be high in two nutrients before triggering a warning could allow several unhealthy products to avoid the label.The Supreme Court questioned the need for such a phased approach during Thursday's hearing."It has to be sugar and salt. Only then will you ask them to put a label?" Justice JB Pardiwala asked the government's lawyer, stressing the word "and".
Additional Solicitor General Brijender Chahar, appearing for FSSAI, said the regulator could now consider implementing both phases together following the court's observation.That could mean a product would carry a red warning if it crosses the limit for even one of the specified nutrients, whether added sugar, salt or saturated fat.
NIN flags gaps in proposed system
The matter has been under the Supreme Court's consideration for months following petitions seeking stronger front-of-pack nutrition warnings. The court had recently given FSSAI a two-week deadline to come back with its proposals.As that deadline approached, the National Institute of Nutrition in Hyderabad submitted its suggestions to the food regulator.NIN has argued that the proposed system should not focus only on added sugar and added fat. It has suggested that factors such as total calories, total sugar and total fat should also be taken into account when deciding whether a packaged food needs a warning.The concern is that looking at only selected nutrients could allow some foods with an unhealthy overall nutritional profile to escape the warning system.A scientist from NIN explained this using fried snacks as an example. A packet of salty fried chips may contain little added sugar and could fall below the proposed threshold for added fat, while still being extremely calorie-dense because of its fat content.Under a system focused only on added sugar and added fat, such a product could therefore avoid a red warning despite being unhealthy when consumed frequently.
Why the labels matter
Front-of-pack nutrition labelling is intended to give consumers an easy-to-understand warning without requiring them to study detailed nutritional information printed on the back of a packet.The proposed red hexagon is designed to work much like a stop sign, with words such as "high fat", "high sugar" or "high salt" clearly displayed depending on which limit a product crosses.
NIN has also pointed out that the nutritional quality of a food cannot necessarily be determined simply by whether it is ultra-processed. A samosa or jalebi, for instance, may be high in fat or sugar without being classified as an ultra-processed food. At the same time, some whole-grain breakfast cereals may be ultra-processed but relatively low in fat, salt and sugar.The debate before the court is therefore not merely about the shape or colour of a label. It is about what nutritional criteria should trigger a warning and whether the proposed system is strong enough to help consumers identify foods that could be harmful when eaten regularly.
