Green leader Zack Polanski aims to catapult himself into the Commons via Starmer’s old seat
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
02:00:00 UTC
11:00:00 KST

LONDON — Keir Starmer’s old seat in the Commons is up for grabs. Zack Polanski is throwing everything at turning the Labour stronghold of Holborn and St. Pancras green.
The leader of the left-wing populist Green Party is almost certain to be selected to stand in the Oct. 8 contest Thursday night, and activists have already flooded constituents with leaflets — with Polanski claiming they delivered 80,000 in just two hours Sunday.
Labour is mounting its defense. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband — a popular figure on the Labour left who fronted a new set of trade sanctions on Israel this week — has already visited the seat, delivering a message of hope to Labour canvassers days after the former British prime minister announced he was standing down.
Advertisement
Holborn and St. Pancras has had a Labour MP since its creation in 1983. The Greens would need to overturn Starmer’s 11,572 vote majority.
For the two main parties in contention in the race to replace Starmer, there is a lot at stake.
What’s at stake for Labour?
This is Andy Burnham’s first test in a parliamentary by-election since becoming prime minister over the summer. For Labour, holding onto Holborn and St. Pancras would send a message that Labour’s image has been successfully divorced from Starmer’s unpopularity. It would also be an encouraging sign voters have accepted him as the new prime minister and are prepared to buy into his plan for government.
The selection on Wednesday night of Camden Council Leader Sagal Abdi-Wali as the Labour candidate — who came to the U.K. as a refugee from Somalia — could also help the party’s chances.
Reform UK spokesperson Zia Yusuf attacked Abdi-Wali’s background when she emerged as the frontrunner, and Labour will likely make the argument for progressive voters to back Abdi-Wali in a show of strength against Nigel Farage’s party.
However, losing a seat that has been deemed safe for so long would be damaging for both Burnham and the party, as it would suggest that the reputational damage Labour suffered under Starmer had stuck.
Advertisement
Sending such a high-profile party figure as the foreign secretary to address campaigners, while canvassers have already hit the streets, is a telling sign in a seat that historically should be a slam dunk for anyone wearing a red rosette.
What’s at stake for Greens?
A win for the Greens could be significant for two reasons. First, if Polanski wins the nomination to be the party’s candidate, it would put party leader in the House of Commons. It would allow them to argue the party still has momentum and has not peaked.
The Gorton and Denton victory in February was the first time the Greens had got an MP into parliament via a by-election. But since Burnham took office, Polanski has had more difficulty cutting through, while a so-called “Burnham bounce” has hit the Greens’ poll ratings.
Green candidate Geraldine Coggins came a disappointing third in the Manchester mayoral election in July, despite a significant ground and social media campaign by the party.
However, a win in London could revitalize the party and show Burnham that he is still at risk of hemorrhaging left-wing support to the Greens unless he listens to certain demands — such as the public ownership of water, a wealth tax, and rent controls.
The fight
Holborn and St. Pancras has never previously been fought as a two-horse race between Labour and the Greens.
Advertisement
Keir Starmer is pictured on the sidelines of the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France on June 16, 2026. | Pool photo by Isabel Infantes via Getty Images
Back in 2024, the Greens did not make a big play for the seat. During that race, it was independent candidate Andrew Feinstein — who later went on to be involved with Jeremy Corbyn and Zarah Sultana’s Your Party project — who posed the biggest threat to Starmer.
Feinstein ran on a pro-Gaza, anti-austerity ticket, and managed to make a dent in the then-PM’s majority, winning 18.9% of the vote.
Feinstein will not run this time, which could mean that his support transfers to the Greens, rather than Labour.
Even then, combined Green and Feinstein support totaled 29%, compared to Starmer’s 49%, at the last general election. Moreover, this time they will not be able to present themselves as a protest vote against Starmer personally.
It would help the Greens if university students are back before the vote as there are dozens of private and university-run accommodation buildings in the areas. But the short election timetable means most will not have moved in before September 22 — the deadline to register to vote.
There’s also a large Muslim community in the seat — around 20% — which both parties will want to attract.
Advertisement
In 2024, the war in Gaza was a major issue that pushed voters away from Labour. Burnham has said that the party’s position under Starmer was wrong, and is taking a stronger stance against the Israeli government. Restrictions on buying goods made in Jewish settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank were announced Tuesday.
The battle lines
The by-election might become a battle of competing national visions. Green supporters argue that Burnham will be prime minister regardless of the outcome, and that having Polanski as an MP will add to pressure on the government in parliament from the left.
Meanwhile, Labour is selling Burnham’s vision for the future. “We can go out in this by-election and really talk with pride about what Andy’s new government in doing,” Miliband told campaigners last weekend. “He has a big argument about how the country needs to change; now it’s up to us in Holborn and St. Pancras to win back the progressive voters.”
The constituency faces a number of specific local challenges. Despite this area of north London often being associated with liberal elite circles, the area is grappling with a housing crisis, high levels of deprivation, and more than a decade of chaos from the stalled HS2 project.
Candidates will have to explain on the doorstep how they would change any of this if elected. Those details may emerge in coming weeks, and crucially during a hustings. But for now, it seems the first stage of battle will be over who can sell the most convincing message of hope.

August declared the hottest month ever recorded
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
02:00:00 UTC
11:00:00 KST

BRUSSELS — August was the joint-hottest month on record globally, official EU data finds, highlighting the worsening effects of global warming.
Average temperatures worldwide temporarily soared to 1.65 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels last month, according to Copernicus, the Earth observation unit of the EU's space program.
The only other time monthly global temperatures hit that level was in July 2023.
Advertisement
Copernicus said the record temperatures were "due to global heating from burning fossil fuels," combined with rising sea surface temperatures in the Pacific linked to a strong El Niño climate pattern.
"Combined with record global sea surface temperatures and the warmest summer on record for western Europe, these observations show how climate change is driving extremes across both the atmosphere and the oceans," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which carried out the research for Copernicus.
The sweltering August capped a record-breaking European summer of heatwaves, wildfires and droughts, as planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions around the world continue to rise.
Global greenhouse gas emissions from human activities last year rose 0.7% to reach a record 54 billion tons of CO2 equivalent, the European Commission said Monday — an annual rate that would likely lock in 1.5 degrees of warming by the end of the decade.
The United States led the upward trend, increasing its climate pollution by 2.2% in 2025.
In China, the world's top climate polluter, emissions rose 0.1% in 2025, while in India they fell 0.2%. The EU's emissions also fell by 0.2% in 2025, the Commission said.
Advertisement
Sea and air
Copernicus' overall figures combine global air and sea surface temperatures.
Global surface air temperatures in August hit 16.96C, the joint-hottest monthly temperature ever recorded and surpassing the 30-year average between 1990 and 2020 by 0.85C.
The average sea surface temperature was at 21.07C, also the joint-hottest on record.
In Europe, August was the fourth-hottest on record, at 1.1C above the 30-year average. Overall, 2026 was Europe's third-hottest summer on record, and the hottest ever recorded in Western Europe.

The video on Wednesday was a surprise for those who attended the conservative gathering in Dallas, Texas, where President Donald Trump is seeking to galvanise support ahead of the November elections.

“Yes, I’m Senator John Fetterman, Pennsylvania. Yes, I’m a Democrat. Why am I here talking to you today? Because, well, I’m a common-sense Democrat,” Fetterman said as he introduced his Republican colleague, Senator Dave McCormick of Pennsylvania.
Fetterman, a 57-year-old first-term senator, has cast himself as an outsider within the Democratic Party.
He has offered outspoken support for Israel and the war on Iran, even as voters and progressive voices in his party criticise those elements of US foreign policy.
“I’m always going to stand with America. I’m always going to reject the extremes and socialism and that anti-American way of life,” Fetterman said in the video clip.
But his appearance at the Republican Party’s first-ever midterm convention is likely to exacerbate criticism from his Democratic colleagues.

His approval rating is now higher among Republicans in Pennsylvania than among members of his own party.
Last month, a poll from The New York Times, Siena College and The Philadelphia Inquirer suggested that 73 percent of Pennsylvania Republicans approved of Fetterman’s performance, up from 25 percent in 2024.
Meanwhile, Democratic support in the state had slid dramatically over the last two years, slipping from 74 percent to 22 percent. Some 63 percent of Democratic respondents held an unfavourable view of him.
While Fetterman has depicted himself as a maverick within the Democratic Party, he has denied that he would switch parties to become a Republican.
“I’m not going to be a Republican, but I’m going to be a Democrat that’s going to have a conversation with whoever is playing it straight,” he said in a recent interview with Fox News.
Still, speculation about Fetterman’s party credentials has continued as the midterms near.
The election on November 3 will decide which party controls Congress for the final two years of Trump’s term.
Republicans currently hold a small majority in the House of Representatives and Senate, but they could face a setback at the polls as voters express frustration over cost of living issues and Trump’s deepening unpopularity.
Still, reclaiming the Senate especially could be an uphill climb for Democrats. Only a third of Senate seats are up for re-election this year, compared with all 435 House seats.
Fetterman is not up for re-election until 2028.

Trump advisers warn Iran war could drag on for years — report
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:50:22 UTC
10:50:22 KST

Senior White House advisers have privately warned US President Donald Trump that the conflict with Iran could continue for years, potentially lasting through the remainder of his term, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.
Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and other senior officials have discussed with Trump the possibility that Tehran could continue resisting US pressure despite a naval blockade, sanctions and military operations, the report said on Wednesday.
The private assessments contrast sharply with Trump's public assurances that the conflict will end soon.
On Wednesday, he told reporters that the war would end "immediately" after the November midterm elections, claiming that "they can't hold out any longer."
The war, now in its seventh month, has killed 18 US service members and raised concerns over military resources and disruptions to global energy markets.
US gasoline prices averaged $4.22 a gallon Wednesday, up from $4.01 a month earlier and $3.19 a year ago, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA).
Trump has repeatedly expressed a desire for a quick resolution while supporting a broader economic campaign against Tehran.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has described the strategy, dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast," as an alternative to major combat operations.
White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales defended the administration's approach, saying: "President Trump has destroyed Iran's military capabilities and is crippling what's left of its abysmal economy with the most powerful naval blockade in world history and crushing sanctions," she added.
"Only President Trump knows what he will do and when."
Vance has also declined to predict when hostilities will end, saying: "It would be irresponsible for us to write out our strategy and our timeline for an Iranian nation that simply cannot honour its commitments and cannot stop shooting at commercial ships."
Decisive results unlikely
The Pentagon is preparing to extend the deployment of some air defence units in the Middle East without a firm end date, while a third Marine Expeditionary Unit is expected to deploy to the region this fall, the report said.
Iran expert Suzanne Maloney of the Brookings Institution said the blockade was unlikely to deliver a decisive result quickly.
"The US naval blockade is unlikely to produce a decisive outcome in the near or even medium term, so the only realistic use of this tool would have to be predicated on plans for a long-term siege," she said.
"Even then, its prospects for success are dubious, mainly because of the unintended consequences," she added.

F1 debuts a new track with a corner so grand it is called Monumental
Unknown

F1 debuts at Madring for Spanish Grand Prix, race start time
In short:
The Spanish Grand Prix will be held in Madrid, as the new Madring circuit.
The 270-degree turn 12, named La Monumental, is the centrepiece of the new track.
What's next?
ABC Sport will have a live blog of the Formula 1 Spanish Grand Prix from 9pm AEST on Sunday, September 13.
Formula 1 debuts a new circuit to its calendar, and despite no grand prix raced yet, the Madring already boasts a corner that is poised to become an iconic scene in motorsport.
The Spanish Grand Prix has moved from Barcelona to the nation's capital, Madrid, with the brand-new Madring contracted to host the event until 2035.
The track uses a combination of public roads and private land and will at times reflect a street circuit, and other times a permanent race track.
But the defining feature of this 22-corner circuit is turn 12: La Monumental.
Turn 12 is a long, banked hairpin that promises to be unlike anything in F1 currently.
The 270-degree curve will have banking up to 13.5 degrees, not as dramatic as the 18-degrees of banking at Zandvoort, but this corner will be taken at much higher speed.
Williams driver Carlos Sainz drove around the circuit earlier this year in a Ford Mustang GT, and said he expects F1 cars to be flying around La Monumental.
"My feeling is the corner is going to be flat out the whole way, and it's going to create an overtaking opportunity into the next tight left," he said.
"The banking will allow you to maybe position the car higher up or lower down if you want to get clean air to follow.
"But if it's easy flat, then it will also be a corner where if you stay tight, you will produce quite a bit of slipstream, like you see in Zandvoort."
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli enters this weekend with a 66-point lead in the drivers' championship over teammate George Russell, after a stunning win in Italy last Sunday despite starting 19th on the grid.
Australian Oscar Piastri is seventh in the drivers' championship, 151 points behind Antonelli, and placed fifth last Sunday at the Italian Grand Prix.

- 9pm: Western Australia

Medvedev anticipates soon ‘peaceful death’ of International Criminal Court
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:43:15 UTC
10:43:15 KST

MOSCOW, September 10. /TASS/. Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev has predicted a soon "peaceful death" of the International Criminal Court (ICC).
According to Medvedev, the ICC is an example of a completely failed model of a court. "Now, practically all countries, including leading ones, except European states, have begun to say that the model this court is based on is flawed," he said in an interview with the Vedomosti daily.
The problem is that the ICC is based on the principle of universal jurisdiction even over those countries that have not signed its founding documents, he explained.
"That is why I think the International Criminal Court will soon die a peaceful death. Good riddance," he added.

Ukraine nearly out of F-16 missiles used to intercept Russian jet-powered drones – The Economist
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
04:39:00 EEST
10:39:00 KST

Ukraine nearly out of F-16 missiles used to intercept Russian jet-powered drones – The Economist
Ukraine is nearly out of US-made AIM-120 and AIM-9 missiles for F-16 fighter jets, which are used to intercept Russian cruise missiles and new jet-powered drones.
Source: The Economist
Details: Ukrainian air defence lacks sufficient missiles to intercept the new Russian Geran-4 and Geran-5 UAVs, which can fly at speeds of up to 600 km/h, while Russia is producing around 3,000 of them a month.
Their turbojet engines are mostly supplied from China, although some components are manufactured directly in Russia using smuggled Western 3D printers. Alongside the larger Banderol drones, these UAVs are increasingly resembling inexpensive cruise missiles, leaving F-16 fighter jets critically short of AIM-120 and AIM-9 missiles to intercept them.
Ukraine is developing its own interceptor drones to counter Russian UAVs, but the situation with defence against ballistic weapons is even more difficult.
Ukraine's stockpile of PAC-3 missiles for Patriot systems is now also nearly depleted. New large-scale deliveries from the US are unlikely because American stockpiles have been depleted by the war with Iran.
Meanwhile, Russia has increased ballistic missile production to around 100 a month: 60 Iskander-M missiles and 40 RM-48U missiles.
There are some expectations surrounding the planned delivery of several older French-Italian SAMP/T air defence batteries, along with Aster missiles, to Ukraine by the end of 2026. Next year, Ukraine is due to receive eight of the latest SAMP/T NG systems.
Quote: "The new system has a more advanced radar for the final stage of guidance and can handle multiple manoeuvring ballistic missiles, such as Russia's Iskander-M. The Aster has a warhead that explodes next to the incoming missile, rather than the PAC-3's 'hit-to-kill' impact. But French army sources claim it outperforms the Patriot in some respects. It is also less than half the US$7m price of the latest export version of the PAC-3."
Details: Germany plans to produce up to 200 less powerful PAC-2 missiles a year under licence, some of which could be supplied to Ukraine with the agreement of NATO countries.
A joint European-Ukrainian project called Freyja is intended to fundamentally change the situation. Its ambition has been compared with that of a "moonshot" programme. Its goal is to provide Ukraine and its European allies with a significantly cheaper and higher-volume alternative to PAC-3 missiles compatible with NATO-standard radars and data-link systems.
The planned interceptor is based on the Ukrainian FP-7 short-range ballistic missile. Sensors, guidance and control systems will be supplied by 12 European defence companies, including France's Thales, Italy's Leonardo, Germany's Diehl and Sweden's Saab.

What is celebrated on September 10 in Ukraine and around the world
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
04:38:12 EEST
10:38:12 KST

What is celebrated on September 10 in Ukraine and around the world
Kyiv • UNN
September 10 marks World Suicide Prevention Day, Teachers' Day in China, and Gibraltar National Day. Believers honor the holy female martyrs.
On September 10, the world observes World Suicide Prevention Day under the auspices of the WHO, Teachers' Day in China, and Gibraltar National Day. According to the new-style church calendar, the holy martyrs Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora are commemorated, while according to the old style, the discovery of the relics of Saint Job of Pochaiv is observed, writes UNN.
World Suicide Prevention Day
An official global initiative founded in 2003 by the International Association for Suicide Prevention (IASP) with the support of the World Health Organization (WHO). The day's aim is to draw public and government attention to suicide as one of the leading causes of premature death worldwide, overcome the stigmatization of mental disorders, and develop accessible systems of psychological support and crisis intervention.
International Makeup Day
An unofficial international observance dedicated to the art of makeup, self-expression through cosmetics, and the history of beauty. The event brings together professional makeup artists, makeup artists for film and theater, beauty bloggers, and makeup enthusiasts, highlighting the role of the beauty industry in contemporary culture and cinematography.
Teachers' Day in China
An official public holiday established in 1985 to raise the social status of teachers and recognize their contribution to the development of society. The date was chosen at the beginning of the academic year, when pupils and students traditionally give teachers flowers and cards and express gratitude for their work.
Gibraltar National Day
The principal national holiday of the British Overseas Territory, established to commemorate the first referendum held on September 10, 1967, in which the residents of Gibraltar voted by a majority to preserve ties with the United Kingdom and rejected the proposal to join Spain. The holiday is marked by mass family festivals, ceremonial rallies, and dressing in the red and white colors of the national flag.
Children's Day in Honduras (Dia del Niño)
An official holiday established in 1953 to protect children's rights, support their harmonious development, and ensure access to quality education and healthcare. On this day, schools, communities, and families organize children's entertainment programs and carnivals and give presents.
St. George's Caye Day in Belize
An official national holiday commemorating the decisive battle of September 10, 1798, during which British settlers and the island's enslaved inhabitants successfully repelled an attack by the Spanish fleet, retaining control over the territory of present-day Belize.
The Commemoration Day of the Holy Martyrs Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora
According to the new calendar, Orthodox and Greek Catholic believers commemorate the holy martyrs Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora—three Christian sisters from Bithynia who, during the reign of Emperor Galerius (the early fourth century), refused to renounce their faith and accepted martyrdom after brutal torture. Saint Paul the Obedient of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra, who lived as an ascetic in the Far Caves of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra in the 13th century, and Saint Joasaph are also commemorated on this day.
According to the old calendar, believers observe the discovery of the relics of Saint Job of Pochaiv (1659)—a prominent Ukrainian Orthodox saint and abbot of the Pochaiv Lavra who, during the religious conflicts of the 17th century, strengthened the Orthodox faith, developed the monastery, and supported printing. The holy martyr Shushanik (Susanna), Princess of Rani, whose martyrdom is described in ancient Georgian literature, is also commemorated.

Iran likely to reverse-engineer captured US underwater drone
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:36:51 UTC
10:36:51 KST

Breadcrumb
Iran likely to reverse-engineer captured US underwater drone
Iran's capture of a US military underwater drone gives Tehran an opportunity to study and potentially reverse engineer the vessel, delivering a setback for the Pentagon and drone maker Anduril.
The US military and Anduril have downplayed the significance of the drone falling into Iranian hands. The vessel, a Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle designed for long-range surveillance and other undersea missions, is among a new generation of military drones intended to operate for days with little human intervention. Washington has previously treated the loss of advanced drones to Iran as a serious matter.
After Iran captured an RQ-170 Sentinel stealth reconnaissance drone in 2011, then-President Barack Obama publicly asked Tehran to return the aircraft. Iran later claimed it had reverse-engineered the drone and subsequently unveiled domestically produced models that appeared to draw heavily on its design.
More recently, the U.S. military moved swiftly to prevent Iranian forces from taking possession of uncrewed maritime technology. In 2022, a US Navy patrol ship and MH-60S Seahawk helicopter were deployed after an Iranian naval vessel attempted to tow away a Saildrone surface vessel in the Gulf, according to the Navy.
Analysts say Iran is unlikely to gain a decisive military advantage from the captured drone, but the episode nonetheless represents a propaganda victory for Tehran and an awkward setback for Washington's efforts to project technological superiority.
Iranian embassies mock US
Iranian embassies around the world have mocked the US for losing its drone. Iran's embassy in Ghana, in a post on X, boasted about picking the submersible up in "a strait controlled by people who can hear a shrimp sneeze," adding that, "Our guys picked it up like a plastic bottle in a fishing net. Fully intact. Still blinking like an idiot. Condolences to whoever was holding the joystick."
US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins of US Central Command said the "defective drone was an older model that neither collected sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment." Anduril did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
"Of course Iran will take every opportunity as a propaganda win," said Farzin Nadimi, a senior fellow at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy. "It can help the (Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps) make better versions of their own designs."
Iran will almost certainly try to pry open the drone's hardware, but the drone's software carries built-in defenses, said Bryan Clark, a senior fellow and director of the Center for Defense Concepts and Technology at the Hudson Institute. Iranian engineers "could definitely reverse-engineer the mechanical systems," he said, pointing to Tehran's track record with captured American aircraft.
"Unboxing ceremony by our reverse engineers, tomorrow morning!" Iran's embassy in Hyderabad wrote on X.
The incident has also highlighted a disconnect between the messaging of Anduril and its customer, the US Navy.
Navy officials said the Dive-LD was an older-model vehicle that suffered a malfunction and was recovered by Iranian forces after being left "dead in the water."
Anduril has promoted the Dive-LD as "the most reliable and flexible" large autonomous underwater vehicle available, saying it is capable of operating for up to 10 days in demanding conditions. In addition to its use by the US Navy, the Dive-LD was the testbed vehicle for the development of Australia's new Ghost Shark large underwater drone.
"This is something that Iran has proven very adept at exploiting for its own benefit in terms of seeking to frame the narrative as one of US, in this case, ineptitude and their ability to sort of retain control over the Strait of Hormuz," said Mona Yacoubian, director of the Middle East program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

Only one-third of Americans trust official election results, distrust of the U.S. government is growing – poll
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
04:35:21 EEST

Only one-third of Americans trust official election results, distrust of the U.S. government is growing – poll
Kyiv • UNN
Americans’ trust in official election results has fallen to 34%, compared with 40% in 2024. About 60% do not trust information from the U.S. government.
Americans are increasingly losing trust in information from the federal government, and ahead of the midterm elections, only 34% of adults are confident in the official certification of their results. This is according to a new survey by the AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research and USAFacts, AP reports, writes UNN.
Details
The share of Americans who "strongly" or "somewhat" trust the official certification of election results has fallen from 40% in 2024 to 34% now. AP notes that the certification process, which was previously largely routine, became politicized after the 2020 presidential election.
The survey also showed an overall decline in trust in information from the federal government compared with previous years, particularly the period of Donald Trump's first presidential term.
About 60% of Americans distrust government information
Approximately 6 in 10 American adults said they have "little" or "no" trust in federal government information on the environment, foreign policy, elections and politics, abortion, and immigration.
Distrust has increased across all topics tracked in similar surveys since 2019. For example, the share of Americans with low trust in government information about education rose from 37% in 2019 to 53% now, with the figure increasing by 9 percentage points in the past year alone.
The study also found a growing partisan divide in assessments of government information. AP links the current trend, in particular, to changes in the federal bureaucracy following Trump's return to the White House.

Mr Hastie says he will not be taking court action, saying he cannot financially win a legal fight when Senator Hanson is "financed by Australia's richest person".
Independent senator Jacqui Lambie has lashed Pauline Hanson as a "bloody coward", demanding she "leave our veterans alone" and remove a One Nation cartoon that repeatedly labels Liberal MP Andrew Hastie a "traitor".
Mr Hastie, a former Special Air Service (SAS) soldier, has escalated his fight with One Nation and accused the party of branding him a traitor to his country after he was subpoenaed to give evidence in a defamation case brought by former SAS corporal Ben Roberts-Smith.
Mr Hastie said One Nation's cartoon was not just an attack on him, but on the more than 20 other SAS veterans called to give evidence in the Federal Court, and the broader veteran community.

Mr Joyce added "democracy is a robust thing" and said Mr Hastie had an "arduous" process ahead of him.

"I do think in our public life we need to have respect for people who have risked their lives for this country," she said.

"I think it's a disgraceful cartoon and it should be removed."

Social media must join the fight against teen suicides
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:30:05 UTC
10:30:05 KST

As we observe World Suicide Prevention Day on September 10, the global community reflects on a sobering reality: suicide remains a leading cause of death among young people. Every year, more than 720,000 people die by suicide – each life a story cut short, a family shattered, a community left to grapple with unbearable loss.
In Hong Kong, the Jockey Club Centre for Suicide Research and Prevention (CSRP) at the University of Hong Kong estimates last year’s suicide rate at 13.0 per 100,000 in the population – a slight improvement from 13.8 in 2024. But let me be clear: this is no cause for complacency. The rate among our young people, 
particularly boys
, remains 
stubbornly high
, and that is where my deepest concern lies.
We can no longer afford to ignore the 
role of social media
 in the mental health crisis facing our teenagers. Social media has become the landscape of modern adolescence. In the United States, reports indicate that up to 95 per cent of adolescents use social media, with over one-third reporting near-constant use. For young people, these digital spaces are not merely entertainment – they are where identities are formed, relationships are navigated and self-worth is measured.
Their impact on mental health deserves attention. For decades, my team at the CSRP has tracked the data, studied the patterns and advocated for evidence-based solutions. The evidence is overwhelming. Excessive use of social media is correlated with poor mental health and deteriorating family relationships. The causes of youth suicide are complex – home and school problems are major, intertwined contributors – but the digital environment has become a significant amplifier of distress.
We have long known that irresponsible media reporting can trigger the 
Werther effect
 – where sensational coverage of suicide leads to imitative behaviour. Social media has made this problem exponentially more complicated. A single post, whether a careless comment or misguided “awareness” message, can reach thousands of vulnerable young people instantly. Specificity in describing methods or locations – even when framed as a warning – drives contagion risk.
Yet the responsibility does not rest solely with individuals. The platforms design their algorithms to maximise engagement, often at the expense of well-being. The recent 
US$18 billion
 settlement by Meta Platforms – agreeing to examine its algorithm design to improve mental health among young users – should be a wake-up call for the industry.

Türkiye’s 2025 PISA results are a ‘success story’ for the world to study: OECD official
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:27:20 UTC
10:27:20 KST

Seyma Guven and Busra Nur Cakmak
10 September 2026•Update: 10 September 2026
Türkiye's performance in the 2025 cycle of the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) is a "success story" that the entire world should study closely, said OECD Director for Education and Skills Andreas Schleicher.
According to a statement by Türkiye's National Education Ministry, Schleicher sent a video message congratulating Türkiye on its achievements in the PISA 2025 cycle.
Congratulating Türkiye's teachers and school administrators, he said: "What you have achieved in this latest round of the OECD's PISA assessment is not just good news for Türkiye, it's a story the world should pay attention to."
At a time when many education systems are facing significant challenges, Türkiye stands out as one of the few countries where student performance improved across all three areas, Schleicher said, noting that average results in mathematics, reading and science increased between 2022 and 2025.
He said the proportion of low-performing students has also declined significantly since 2015, demonstrating Türkiye's success in equipping more young people with the foundational skills needed for lifelong learning and future opportunities.
‘We are seeing a school system that is truly on the move'
Stressing that the results were not merely the outcome of one successful year, Schleicher said: "We are seeing a school system that is truly on the move.”
Education is where a country writes the blueprint for its future, he said, adding that the students sitting in Türkiye's classrooms today will shape the country's future as engineers, entrepreneurs, doctors, researchers, teachers and public servants.
Schleicher said there were other reasons to be optimistic about Türkiye's education story, noting that seven out of every 10 students in the country said their teachers take a close interest in their learning, continue explaining material until students understand it, and provide additional support when they need it most.
Students also reported a more positive learning environment in their classrooms compared with a decade ago, he said, stressing that education is not simply a mechanical exchange between a teacher transmitting knowledge and a student receiving it but a human process.
Schleicher said there were also encouraging signs in Turkish students' attitudes toward learning.
According to PISA data, many students are eager to discover new things, are able to persevere when things become difficult and believe that ability can be developed through effort, feedback and practice, he said.
Qualities such as curiosity, perseverance, agency and a growth mindset have become essential foundations for success in learning, work and life in a world where knowledge is changing rapidly and artificial intelligence can generate answers within seconds, he added.
'Türkiye's most valuable natural resource is talent, imagination and potential in its classrooms'
Referring to PISA results showing that Turkish students enthusiastically use digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, Schleicher said the government, recognizing this potential, has made addressing shortages of devices a priority and that this could translate into a significant advantage for the future.
He stressed that the relationship between technology and learning depends on how technology is used, adding that the ultimate purpose of technology should not be to make processes easier but to make learners more capable.
Congratulating Türkiye's education community on the results, Schleicher said the opportunity ahead was to continue moving faster and further while ensuring that every child is included in that journey.
"Türkiye's most valuable natural resource is the talent, imagination and potential sitting in your classrooms today," he said.

Spain’s spy agency warned of mass crossings into Ceuta before border crisis
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:26:46 UTC
10:26:46 KST

Spain’s spy agency warned of mass crossings into Ceuta before border crisis
Declassified documents show Madrid and Morocco were warned of plans by migrants to breach Ceuta border before crisis in July.
Spain’s intelligence services had warned of possible mass crossings by migrants and asylum seekers into Ceuta just before tens of thousands of people arrived in the Spanish enclave in late July, according to declassified documents.
The trove of 40 documents was released on Wednesday amid near-daily protests in Ceuta over the Spanish government’s handling of the crisis, as well as questions over neighbouring Morocco’s role in the events.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Spain’s PM says no evidence Morocco planned Ceuta border rush
- list 2 of 4Morocco’s ruling allies turn on each other before election campaign begins
- list 3 of 4Tens of thousands rally across Spain over Ceuta migrant crisis
- list 4 of 4Which countries banned goods from settlements but trade with Israel?
The documents show that on July 29 – a day before more than 72,000 people began pouring into Ceuta from Morocco – Spain’s National Intelligence Center (CNI) sent an alert via WhatsApp to the Spanish government’s delegation in the city about calls on social media “for an assault on the fence and by sea tomorrow at 8 pm”.
“There are two different groups with a total of 180,000 followers,” the declassified message said, referencing social media groups, “just to give you an idea of its scale”.
On the same day, CNI also warned Moroccan intelligence agencies DGST and DGED of plans for migrants to enter Ceuta by climbing the border fence or swimming around it. The agency mentioned that the plans could take advantage of Morocco’s national Throne Day, celebrated on July 30.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Wednesday rejected the idea that the declassified documents revealed there was prior warning of a border crisis on the scale of what took place between July 30 and 31.
“The existence of this campaign was known to other institutions and was being monitored, but in no way did it constitute or could it be interpreted as an indicator of the scale, nature, or probability of what happened afterward”, Sanchez wrote on X.
There was no immediate comment from Morocco.
Sanchez had previously said there was no evidence of Morocco’s involvement in the crisis, despite a leaked police report in July that alleged “total permissiveness” from Moroccan police during the border rush.
A declassified document issued by CNI at midday on July 30 states that it is “highly likely that the Moroccan authorities are not actively encouraging the migratory wave, but have so far acted in a negligent and passive manner”.
It said that, “at the operational level, no proactive response from Moroccan authorities was observed regarding the loss of control over the situation, beyond the deployment of a few riot control units”.
In the same note, it said many people on the night of July 29 were already “waiting to jump into the water to reach Ceuta”.
“The increased presence of Moroccan police and gendarmes proved insufficient to control the crowd, and, that night, several hundred migrants swam across,” it said.
About 5,000 migrants and asylum seekers, including 1,200 minors, still remain in Ceuta, more than a month after the mass crossing, according to the Spanish government. Local officials cite a higher figure of up to 10,000 people.
The population of Cuba is about 84,000 people.
Madrid has pledged $357m in aid as some remain unhoused in the small city.
The opposition, meanwhile, has accused the government of failing to act despite having been alerted.
“The government knew everything that was happening… They had the information. They are directly responsible for the invasion of Ceuta,” Ester Munoz, spokeswoman for the right-wing Popular Party in parliament, told reporters.

China wife exposes husband’s US$1.5 million insurance-buying affair involving 180 hotel stays

A Chinese man’s seven-year affair with an insurance agent has ignited a legal dispute, revealing dramatic details uncovered by his wife.
Guo, from Liuzhou in Guangxi province, southern China, is married to Zhen, with whom he shares a two-year-old daughter, according to Hongxing News.
In 2017, Zhen discovered flirtatious messages exchanged between her husband and Li, an insurance agent eight years his junior. These texts included “I miss you” and multiple transfers of 520 yuan (US$77), a figure widely associated with “I love you” in Chinese due to its phonetic similarity.
Years later, while hospitalised in 2024, Zhen discovered that Guo had bought medical insurance policies for her and their daughter. This revelation raised suspicions that Guo and Li had continued their relationship.
Zhen later calculated that Guo had transferred over 3 million yuan (US$447,000) to Li over the course of the seven years.
Insurance records indicated that he had acquired more than 50 policies through Li, paying over 10 million yuan (US$1.5 million) in premiums. During this period, Li was promoted to manager in her insurance firm.

At least five killed, 87 missing after ferry fire in Philippines

Deadly Philippines ferry fire leaves dozens missing
At least five people died and dozens were unaccounted for Thursday after a ferry caught fire off the Philippine island province of Palawan, with 43 passengers and crew rescued so far. Coast guard teams continued search and rescue operations as officials worked to establish what happened.
A fire burned overnight on a passenger ferry off the western Philippines, leaving dozens of people missing Thursday and killing at least five.
So far, 43 people have been rescued, coast guard spokeswoman Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said. The ferry MV June Aster was afloat but listing after the fire, which started Wednesday evening, was put out. Tendrils of smoke still wafted over the charred vessel by midday.
Read moreMajor quake off Philippines kills at least 31, triggers tsunami warnings
“We are continuing search and rescue operations,” she said, with a coast guard ship and high-speed response boats joined by a military vessel and other government boats, private volunteers and fishermen.
The coast guard made a radio broadcast to ships nearby to be on the lookout for passengers of the ferry. It has also coordinated with coastal villages in case some passengers drifted to the shore.
Images of the nighttime rescue efforts showed coast guard personnel tossed life jackets to survivors as the ferry burned in the background. Passengers were helped into smaller boats taking them to shallow water, and body bags were laid out at what looked like a port.
The ferry had sailed from the capital Manila and was near its destination of Coron in Palawan province when the fire started around 6:45pm Wednesday.
Bad weather and big waves challenged rescuers. The ferry was around 4 nautical miles (7.4 kilometers) off Coron’s village of Turda when it sent a distress signal but strong sea currents had dragged it to a distance of 7.68 nautical miles (14.2 kilometers) off Turda.
Cayabyab said it was unclear what caused the fire, which one survivor said may have begun in the cargo hold, and the coast guard was coordinating with the shipping company and maritime authorities to get more details.
She said 134 people were on board, 117 of them passengers and 17 crew. There was no information about any foreigners onboard.
Ferries are a common transportation method in the Philippine archipelago. Sea accidents are not uncommon due to storms, badly maintained vessels, overcrowding and spotty enforcement of safety regulations, especially in remote provinces.

In 1987, the ferry Dona Paz sank after colliding with a fuel tanker in the central Philippines, killing more than 4,300 people in the world’s deadliest peacetime maritime disaster.

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Ministry of National Defense tracked 18 Chinese military aircraft, eight naval vessels, and one official ship around Taiwan between 6 a.m. on Wednesday and 6 a.m. on Thursday.
Thirteen of the 18 People’s Liberation Army aircraft crossed the Taiwan Strait median line in the country’s northern, central, southwestern, and eastern air defense identification zone, according to the MND.
In response, the MND deployed aircraft, naval ships, and coastal-based missile systems to monitor PLA activity.

Gray zone tactics are defined as “an effort or series of efforts beyond steady-state deterrence and assurance that attempts to achieve one’s security objectives without resort to direct and sizable use of force.”

RIYADH, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- CyberHero x Riyadh, a humanoid robot combat event, was held in the Saudi capital on Wednesday night, with Team FBA defeating Team AL Majd 4-3 after seven rounds to claim the title.
Described by organizers as the Middle East's first humanoid robot combat event, the nearly two-hour competition featured two robots engaging in physical combat inside a purpose-built octagonal arena under the control of their operators.
The two sides split the opening six rounds to leave the contest tied at 3-3. In the decisive seventh round, Team FBA's robot knocked down its opponent with a powerful kick to seal the victory.
The competition featured T800 humanoid robots developed by Chinese robotics company EngineAI. According to organizers, each robot stands 1.73 meters tall, weighs between 75 and 85 kilograms and has 29 articulated joints.
During the bouts, the robots punched, kicked, jumped, defended and recovered from falls, with their ability to maintain balance after repeated physical contact and quickly resume movement proving an important factor.
According to event organizer Hero Esports, CyberHero incorporates elements of professional sports competition, including knockout decisions, damage statistics and round highlights.
"CyberHero was born from a bold idea about the future of competition: that robots can be pushed to test their limits, break new boundaries and improve through data generated in competition," said Danny Tang, co-founder and CEO of Hero Esports.
Tang said the company hopes competitive scenarios can help test and advance robotics technology.
"That is one of the lessons we have learned from esports, and it is also a responsibility we see for Hero Esports over the next decade -- to use competition to drive innovation and progress," she said.
Tang added that Hero Esports is establishing a global technology lab at its Shanghai headquarters to bring together technical expertise and talent from around the world.
Prince Faisal bin Bandar bin Sultan Al Saud, chairman of the Saudi Esports Federation, welcomed the decision to stage the first CyberHero event in Riyadh.
"This is testament to the passion of our fans and Saudi Arabia's ongoing commitment to esports as a thriving sector and entertainment choice," he said, adding that the event had created "new boundaries for audience experience and competition."
According to organizers, CyberHero's inaugural season is planned to visit eight cities across four regions: the Middle East, Europe, the Americas and Asia, with two stops scheduled for the Middle East.
The Riyadh event opened the series and showcased its competition format ahead of planned events in other regions. ■

BERLIN, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Ermedin Demirovic scored a 13-minute hat-trick as VfB Stuttgart beat Norwegian champions Viking FK 3-1 at home to claim their first-ever victory in a Champions League opener on Wednesday.
The visitors made the more threatening start, with Kristoffer Askildsen and Henrik Bjordal producing the first attempts, while Stuttgart initially struggled to create openings despite seeing plenty of the ball.
That changed with their first clear chance in the 20th minute. Angelo Stiller delivered from the byline and Demirovic converted from close range, the ball going in off the underside of the crossbar.

Demirovic became the first Stuttgart player to score three goals in a single match in either the Champions League or its predecessor, the European Cup.
Viking pushed higher after the restart and enjoyed their strongest spell without seriously reducing Stuttgart's advantage. Tripic had an effort blocked before Chris Fuhrich sent a free kick narrowly over at the other end, while Jeff Chabot made an important intervention as the visitors continued to press.
Stuttgart regained greater control after the hour mark and managed their two-goal cushion through the closing stages.
Stuttgart's next Champions League match is a visit to Slovan Bratislava in mid-October.
"The three points were what mattered today. We could have played better, but we also must be happy to be back in the Champions League and to have won," said Demirovic. "There were a few situations where we allowed them too much, and our coach will not be happy about that." ■

Advanced technology boosts conservation, restoration of Terracotta Warriors in NW China's Shaanxi
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
09:21:32 CST
10:21:32 KST

Restoration specialists piece together a terracotta warrior at the on-site conservation lab of the Pit No.1 of the Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum in Xi'an, northwest China's Shaanxi Province, Sept. 3, 2026.
At the world-famous Terracotta Warriors site in Xi'an, visitors can now witness a once behind-the-scenes process -- experts meticulously restoring over 2,000-year-old clay soldiers. At the newly launched conservation lab in Pit No. 1, specialists piece fragmented pottery together manually, reviving scattered relics into solemn and life-size warriors.
The lab officially opened in 2024, celebrating the 50th anniversary of the discovery and excavation of the iconic Terracotta Warriors. A professional excavation and preservation facility in Pit No. 2 was also completed and put into operation. The two facilities form a full-cycle conservation system covering excavation, transportation, restoration and storage.
This advanced system greatly improves the protection of the warriors' original pigments. Buried underground for over 2,000 years, the Terracotta Warriors suffered severe damage from fires, soil collapses and underground water fluctuations, with most original colors fading away over time. Previously, surviving paint layer would easily curl, peel or flake off once exposed to drastic environmental changes after excavation. Today, newly unearthed painted relics are directly transferred to the on-site lab. Through keeping stable humidity control, ultrasonic inspection, 3D scanning, professional cleaning and reinforcement treatment, researchers now do their utmost to preserve the warriors' ancient original hues. SHANGHAI, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China Business Report released on Thursday by the American Chamber of Commerce in Shanghai (AmCham Shanghai) showed a sharp rebound in business confidence among its surveyed member companies operating in China.
Business confidence bounced back markedly, with 58 percent of respondents now optimistic about China's five-year business outlook, up by 17 percentage points year over year, said the report.
Profitability rebounded to the highest since 2019, with 78 percent of respondents profitable in 2025, a 7 percentage-point increase from the previous year, according to the report. ■

Argentina to file criminal complaint against Israeli drilling company for operating in Falklands
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:21:17 UTC
10:21:17 KST

Argentina’s government announced on Monday that it will file a criminal complaint against Navitas Petroleum, an Israeli oil company, for operating in the Falklands.
The announcement came from Argentine President Javier Milei’s office and included complaints against several petroleum companies operating in the area.
According to the announcement, Navitas has been operating under the license of the United Kingdom's "illegitimate government," with the complaint aiming to "protect natural resources and safeguard the sovereignty of the Argentine Republic over the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, and the corresponding maritime and insular spaces, as they are an integral part of the national territory."
The status of the Falkland Islands is disputed between Argentina and the UK, with both claiming sovereignty over the territory.
The complaint follows a January report by N12 News that Argentina reportedly delayed moving its embassy to Jerusalem because of bilateral tensions over Navitas’s plans to drill oil from a field near the Falkland Islands.
Argentina: Navitas's plan to drill 'unilateral and illegitimate'
The Argentine Foreign Ministry said in December that Navitas, along with partner British company Rockhopper Exploration, had not obtained the proper permits and that their plans were “unilateral and illegitimate.”
The ministry warned of “potentially irreversible future consequences” if the plan proceeds, with both companies banned from drilling in Argentina for drilling without a permit.
Argentine sources told N12 at the time that they considered the plan to be “the theft of a natural resource that belongs to them.”
Mathilda Heller contributed to this report.

New international initiative to combat antisemitism announced by Israel's UN ambassador
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:21:11 UTC
10:21:11 KST

A new initiative to combat antisemitism was launched on Wednesday by Israeli United Nations Ambassador Danny Danon ahead of the upcoming UN secretary-general election.
“The words 'Never Again' were not meant to be a slogan," said Danon. "They were meant to be a commitment. Words, declarations, and statements are not enough to fight the rising antisemitism on the streets, in synagogues, in universities, and even here at the United Nations."
The move, which comes as antisemitism rises around the world, aims to explore ways to turn statements and condemnations into coordinated international action.
The initiative involved the identification of emerging antisemitic threats, as well as the development of tools and policies to combat the threats. Participating countries will coordinate diplomatic efforts to achieve these goals.
"It is time for action," Danon declared. "We thank the countries who have already committed to joining us on this important mission. This mission is not the responsibility of Israel and the Jewish people alone. It is the responsibility of the entire international community."
Danon pushes for prioritization of fight against antisemitism
Danon called for the prioritization of the fight against antisemitism when the international body chooses its next secretary-general, further requesting that more countries join the initiative.
US Ambassador to the UN Jeff Bartos also spoke at the initiative's announcement event, saying the world is "facing a global pandemic of antisemitism."
"That is irrefutable," he emphasized. "Here at the United Nations, special rapporteurs who represent this organization are staining its reputation, its dignity, and discrediting the important work of other UN workers".
Also speaking at the event, EU Coordinator on Combating Antisemitism Katharina von Schnurbein described the fact that many Jews feel the need to hide their identities as Jews as "fully unacceptable."
"There can be no excuse for antisemitism," she said. "It cannot be tolerated anytime or any place."

Israel's Dan Brand rebounds in US Open doubles after cramping ends singles run
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:21:10 UTC
10:21:10 KST

For a few hours on Monday, it looked as though Israeli junior Dan Brand was about to write the same comeback story he had produced one day earlier at the US Open.
Instead, his second-round singles match became a heartbreaking lesson in just how quickly the fortunes of a young tennis player can change, and how much support can mean when they do.
Facing fellow 17-year-old American Andy Johnson, the tournament’s No. 10 seed and the world’s No. 12 junior, Brand again dropped the opening set before fighting his way back. But this time, just as he appeared to have seized control, severe cramping throughout his body brought his singles run to an abrupt end.
Brand lost the first set 6-2 in 28 minutes, going down 2-0 before beginning to find his rhythm in the second. He raised the intensity of his play, became more aggressive and began dictating the pace, winning four consecutive games to take a 4-2 lead before closing out the set 6-3.
It was almost a carbon copy of Sunday’s first-round match, when Brand had also quickly dropped the opening set before battling back to win the next two.
With the momentum and a partisan crowd firmly on his side, Brand appeared poised to mount another comeback.
But Johnson held serve to open the third set and then broke Brand for a 2-0 lead. With Brand trailing 2-0 and facing a 40-30 deficit, he suddenly clutched his right elbow and went to his corner to towel off. He returned to serve underhanded, lost the final point of the game and fell behind 3-0.
Brand then called for a three-minute medical timeout. A trainer evaluated him, had him lie down on the court, and appeared to treat his calf.
Brand would later explain that he was experiencing cramping throughout his body rather than dealing with an injury. He said he had experienced similar cramping before.
When he returned, he managed only two points over the next three games, serving some points underhanded, as Johnson closed out the decisive third set 6-0.
Jewish fans rally around Israeli junior
Yet even as the singles match slipped away, the support around Brand only grew louder.
The enthusiastic, heavily pro-Brand crowd was visibly disappointed and concerned for the young Israeli. Many remained afterward, waiting to take even more photographs and collect more autographs than they had following Sunday’s match.
A number of spectators were visibly Jewish, wearing yarmulkes and skirts. Some had read about Brand in the Jerusalem Post, while others had simply heard his name and “Israel” announced on the tournament schedule and made their way to Court 6 for the fourth match of the day.
Eli Shaer of Great Neck, Long Island, was there with his two children, nieces and nephews, and was among those cheering Brand on.
“He is incredible,” Shaer said after Brand’s second-set comeback. “He is very strong offensively, and he shows Jewish pride.”
Shaer was also struck by the size of the crowd for a junior match.
“It is over 50% full, and they are all here for Dan,” he said.
Martin Friedman of Staten Island, New York, attended with three friends, drawn to the match by a sense of Jewish pride.
“From far away, you smell family on the side court,” Friedman said. “You want to support our nation and our brethren, we are one big happy family.”
Brand faces one of world's top juniors
Brand was facing a formidable opponent. Johnson, ranked No. 12 in the world among juniors, has already competed as a professional and made history in February when he became the youngest player to win an ITF World Tennis Tour men’s singles title since Carlos Alcaraz did so in July 2019. Johnson won the M15 Sunrise, Florida tournament at 16 years and 176 days.
The statistics reflected a competitive match despite the difficult ending. Both players reached serves of 119 mph, with Johnson averaging 94 mph and Brand 91 mph. Neither player recorded an ace. Brand finished with 39 unforced errors to Johnson’s 20.
For Brand, however, there was little time to dwell on the loss.
Brand rebounds with US Open doubles victory
After resting and rehydrating, he returned to the court Tuesday for the doubles competition, teaming with 18-year-old Austrian Thilo Behrman, the world’s No. 6 junior in both singles and doubles. The pair entered the tournament as the No. 5 seed and faced Connor Doig of the Republic of South Africa and Dimitar Kisimov of Bulgaria in the opening round.
This time, Brand walked away with a victory.
Brand and Behrman defeated Doig and Kisimov 6-3, 6-3 in just over an hour, advancing to the round of 16.
Watching from the coach’s box was Robert Raguz, who has been coaching Brand and a cohort of promising international juniors as part of the Grand Slam Player Development program. Raguz has been impressed by the Israeli’s ability to read and adjust to his opponents.
“He is very good at adapting to find his opponent’s weakness, and he has a high tennis IQ,” Raguz said.
The coach believes Brand’s next steps are to develop greater intensity and find more opportunities to train against high-level practice partners who can push him.
For Brand, the doubles victory offered an immediate opportunity to put Monday’s disappointment behind him – while continuing to enjoy an experience he clearly does not want to end.
“The experience here is amazing, the atmosphere is crazy, there are a lot of people, I like it!” Brand said.
He has particularly enjoyed seeing Jewish and Israeli fans filling the stands and cheering him on.
And with Behrman, Brand believes he has found a doubles partner with whom he can continue building something special.
“We are a good team together and hope to continue tomorrow,” Brand said.
The next challenge will come against Yannik Alvarez of Puerto Rico and Ryan Cozad of the United States in the round of 16.
After a painful singles exit, Brand has already shown that he is ready to get back on the court and keep playing.

British-Somaliland group slams UK government over Israel policy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:21:07 UTC
10:21:07 KST

British members of a Somaliland-Israel friendship movement criticized the UK government's policies toward Israel and said they had urged their community not to vote for the governing party, according to a statement sent to The Jerusalem Post.
The statement, issued under the name of the Somaliland-Israel Friendship & Abrahamic Movement's UK branch, said its British members wished to "make our position clear."
"We strongly criticize the current policies of this UK government towards Israel," the statement read. "These policies do not represent the will of the British people living in the UK."
The group described Israel and the United Kingdom as "inseparable brothers," citing a relationship built on history, shared values, democracy, and efforts to promote peace and stability in the Middle East.
The statement further accused the current UK government of abandoning the relationship and adopting what it called an "outdated, double-standard policy."
"Therefore, we as British-Somalilanders have suggested to our community not to vote for this party that is currently in power, because it has opposed Israel and betrayed the true friendship between our two nations," the statement said.
"We stand with Israel. Yesterday, today, and forever," it added.
The statement was signed by Eng. Ahmed Abdillahi Dirie.
UK-Israel relations strained over settlement sanctions
The statement comes amid heightened tensions between Israel and the United Kingdom following new British measures targeting Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced on Tuesday an import ban on goods from what Britain considers illegal settlements in the West Bank, as well as sanctions targeting certain individuals and businesses providing services connected to settlement expansion.
Miliband said during his announcement that he was "unwavering in [his] support for the state of Israel," while maintaining his support for a Palestinian state.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended the measures in parliament on Wednesday, calling the decision an example of British "leadership on the world stage."
Miliband also defended the sanctions on Wednesday, saying he was "proud" of the decision because "it was the right thing to do."
Israel responds to UK measures
In response to the British measures, Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar announced that Israel would close the UK's consulate in east Jerusalem and expel British representatives from the Civil-Military Coordination Center (CMCC) in Kiryat Gat.
Israel's countermeasures also included ending British training of Palestinian Authority security forces in Ramallah and banning 12 British elected representatives and other British nationals from entering Israel.
Sa'ar said that Israel had "nothing against the British people" and maintained that Israel had many friends in Britain while sharply criticizing the policies of the current British government.
The Somaliland-Israel relationship has also expanded in recent months. Somaliland opened its embassy in Jerusalem in June during President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi's first official visit to Israel following the establishment of diplomatic relations between Israel and Somaliland last year.

Dementia prevention too heavily focused on personal choices, study finds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:16:13 UTC
10:16:13 KST

Dementia prevention measures need to be broader in scope, researchers say
In short:
A study has found that a broader approach is needed in order to prevent dementia.
There has been a focus on the choices individuals make, which researchers say has led to environmental and socio-economic factors being overlooked.
What's next?
It is hoped that the research will help to inform prevention policy.
Personal preventative measures alone will not decrease the risk of dementia, researchers have found.
Until now there has been a focus on personal choices such as eating, exercise, social activity and mental health to prevent Australia's leading cause of death.
But a Dementia Australia-funded research paper from Curtin University has found that such efforts may have led to the social, environmental and policy influences that shape brain health being overlooked.
In 2024, a landmark study identified 14 potentially modifiable risk factors for dementia, including high blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol, physical inactivity, smoking and hearing loss.
It found many must be tackled in midlife and could potentially prevent 45 per cent of dementia cases.
In the new paper published in the peer-reviewed medical journal The Lancet, researchers mapped 61 risk factors ranging from lifestyle to socio-economic status.
Of those, 49 (80 per cent) were at the individual level. Far fewer related to the interpersonal or societal levels.
The researchers found far less attention was paid to education, housing, neighbourhood safety, healthcare access, clean air and social connections, "despite growing evidence these factors affect people’s ability to protect their brain health".
"For example, we tell people they need to be physically active, but being physically active can depend on having a safe environment and access to places that are safe to exercise in and affordable," study author Jennifer Dunne said.
“[The 14 factors] are obviously important for a range of reasons, but our study shows that many of the factors that shape dementia risk do not sit solely within an individual’s control."
University of NSW cognitive disorder researcher Simone Reppermund, who was not involved in the study, said the paper highlighted the need for greater understanding of the role sociological, economic and environmental factors played in dementia prevention.
"Often the message goes out that it is actually on the individual to change something, but many important factors that actually are very much interlinked and interconnected with these individual behaviours are neglected or not even looked at in research, and especially in policy," she said.
"This is harder to do because it changes from society to society, and then you have high-income and low-income countries, but it is definitely an important way to go forward."
About 446,500 people are living with dementia in Australia and that figure is projected to exceed one million by 2065, according to Dementia Australia.
Dementia is the decline in the ability to think, remember and reason to the extent that it interferes with a person's daily life and activities, the National Ageing Research Institute said.
"There is a lot more focus now on dementia and how to prevent it, because dementia is a huge economic burden, a huge health burden, and it affects not only the individual but the whole family and the whole society," Dr Reppermund said.
Dr Dunne said it hoped the latest research findings would inform prevention policy.
"The research has been very valuable to get us to this point," she said.
"What we're now saying is that it does need to go further, and that if we really want to be talking about preventing dementia and improving brain health at a population level, we need ot look at the whole population and how the individual lives within that."

UK right-wing protesters target Pakistan cricket team hotel
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:11:15 UTC
10:11:15 KST

Breadcrumb
UK anti-migrant protesters mistakenly target Pakistan U-19 cricket team hotel
Anti-migrant demonstrators in southern England massed outside a hotel where Pakistan's Under-19 cricket team were staying after mistaking them for asylum seekers, British media reported Wednesday.
The incident Tuesday evening in a northern suburb of Portsmouth occurred some 48 hours after protesters disrupted the disembarkation of scores of migrants near the port city and confronted police in widely condemned scenes.
Immigration and the arrival of tens of thousands of asylum seekers annually on small boats from mainland Europe has become a politically toxic issue in Britain, sparking numerous protests in recent years, some turning violent.
Tuesday's incident came after reports online about a coach with young Asian men on board being seen at a Marriott Hotel in the Portsmouth suburb of Cosham drew protestors to the venue, according to media reports.
A councillor from anti-immigration party Reform UK went to the scene and helped disperse the crowd after confirming the men were in fact members of Pakistan's teenage cricket team, The Guardian newspaper said.
The senior Pakistan men's side are currently involved in the third Test against England at Birmingham's Edgbaston ground.
A spokesman for Hampshire Police -- which is responsible for the region -- said the force "were notified that a group of people were starting to congregate" near the hotel Tuesday evening.
"Officers subsequently attended and spoke to members of the public that had gathered who were expressing concerns about a coach that had been seen in the area," the spokesman added.
"The officers explained that their concerns were not correct," the spokesman said, without confirming the Pakistani cricketers were the mistaken target.
He noted the crowd of around 30 people dispersed a short time later and no offences were identified.
Michael Bradley, a national organiser from the Stand Up To Racism organisation, condemned the incident as showing "where the scapegoating of refugees and migrants can lead".
"When a Pakistan U-19's team is faced by protests because it 'might' in fact be a group of migrants it means that effectively any group of black or Asian people coming into the city are being seen by the far right as a potential target," he said.
"It's obvious where all this is going to end -- racist attacks and more violence."

Baby orangutans found in forest in India spark trafficking investigation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:10:57 UTC
10:10:57 KST

Five baby orangutans have been found in a forest in India, prompting authorities to investigate if they were trafficked into the country from south-east Asia.
The orangutans, native only to the islands of Borneo and Sumatra and known for their shaggy red fur, were found in Balasore district of Odisha state, thousands of kilometres away from their natural habitat.
Odisha’s environment minister, Ram Singh Khuntia, said wildlife investigators were trying to establish how the rare apes reached India.
“We suspect that an international racket might be involved in this,” Singh said.
International commercial trade in orangutans is prohibited under Cites – a global agreement governing trade in endangered wildlife.
The five babies were found by forest department officials who were patrolling in the Jaleswar range in Balasore district.
Officials believed the orangutans had been in the area for just a few days, and they have now been placed in quarantine at a zoological park in Odisha.
According to the World Wildlife Fund, about 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago.
The Tapanuli orangutan (Pongo tapanuliensis), a third species, is classified as critically endangered, with fewer than 800 believed to survive in the wild.
In November, conservationists found the Tapanuli population had been reduced by 7% after severe flooding in Indonesia.
Between 33 and 54 Tapanuli orangutans were estimated to have been killed in widespread floods and landslides in North Sumatra province.
Previous research has suggested annual losses of 1% of the Tapanuli orangutan population would be sufficient to lead to eventual extinction.
The entire Tapanuli population dwells solely in the West Block of the Batang Toru, a forest threatened by mining, palm oil plantations and a large hydropower project.

OpenAI math breakthrough sparks controversy
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-10
01:07:30 UTC
10:07:30 KST

OpenAI math breakthrough sparks controversy
OpenAI has come under fire after claiming its AI solved one of mathematics’ most famous problems. Researchers are raising questions over how the company arrived at the breakthrough, while others are accusing it of exaggerating the achievement to boost valuation ahead of a potential IPO.
The company announced on Tuesday that an internal AI system had solved the Navier-Stokes problem, one of mathematics’ famous Millennium Prize questions. It concerns equations describing how liquids and gases move and asks whether the math can suddenly break down under certain conditions. A correct solution carries a $1 million prize from the Clay Mathematics Institute.
OpenAI said around 10,000 AI agents worked on the problem for roughly 88 hours, exchanging millions of messages and generating around 130 billion output tokens before producing a computer-verified proof.
The company says the result satisfies the official wording of the prize problem, although it does not intend to claim the money. It also presented the feat as evidence of how rapidly its internal AI systems are advancing.
The announcement has drawn mixed reactions, with some calling it an “exciting day for mathematics” while others have raised suspicions of plagiarism and questioned the significance of the achievement.
NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster has accused OpenAI of throwing massive resources at the problem only after learning that he and Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge were making progress on a related approach.
Mathematicians have also cautioned against declaring the problem solved before the proof is independently examined. Diego Cordoba, whose work helped pioneer the approach used by the AI, said a valid solution would be a “big surprise.”
Others have been far more critical. Prominent tech commentator Mehdi, who has a large following on X, opened a lengthy attack on the announcement by telling OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to “go f**k yourself,” before accusing the company of trying to “privatize the very mechanism of human knowledge.”
Mehdi argued that OpenAI had tackled an easier version of the problem and used brute-force computing rather than genuine machine reasoning or scientific intuition.
He suggested that the supposed breakthrough was achieved by thousands of AI agents simply searching mathematical ground already explored by human researchers in order to manufacture an artificial “Sputnik moment” to boost excitement around its technology and inflate its valuation ahead of a stock-market listing.
OpenAI has acknowledged that the project began after hearing rumors that outside mathematicians had made progress on related problems but has denied accessing their unpublished work. At the same time, it said it could not rule out that anonymized data from their use of OpenAI products had helped improve its models.
